items.stem: Light of wavelength 450 nm from a collimated green DPSS diode-pumped laser directed normally onto two narrow parallel slits illuminates a double slit of slit separation 0.24 mm in which each slit has finite width 0.06 mm. On a screen 2.2 m away, what is the full linear width of the central single-slit diffraction envelope?
items.workedSolution: The first single-slit diffraction minima lie at θ = ±λ / b, so the full width of the central diffraction envelope on the screen is w_env = 2λD / b = (2 × 4.50 × 10⁻⁷ × 2.2) / 6.00 × 10⁻⁵ = 0.0330 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses w_env = 2λD / b to obtain 0.0330 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes the adjacent interference fringe spacing λD / d instead of the diffraction envelope width 2λD / b.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes slit separation d in place of individual slit width b, computing 2λD / d.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the half-width λD / b from the centre to one minimum instead of the full width 2λD / b.

items.stem: On a precision wire-tension metrology rig with rigid end collets of length 1.5 m, transverse waves propagate at 192 m s⁻¹. What is the resonant frequency when the string vibrates in its n = 6 harmonic mode?
items.workedSolution: For a string fixed at both ends in harmonic n = 6, λ_n = 2L / n = 2(1.5) / 6 = 0.500 m. Thus f_n = v / λ_n = 192 / 0.500 = 384 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Applies f_n = nv / (2L) to obtain 384 Hz (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the first-harmonic fundamental frequency v / (2L) instead of multiplying by harmonic number n.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the closed-one-end pipe formula nv / (4L) instead of fixed-both-ends nv / (2L).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in λ_n = 2L / n, computing f = nv / L.

items.stem: During a straight-line Doppler measurement in still air (sound speed 340 m s⁻¹), a fire-appliance warning horn sounding at 700 Hz moves away from the observer at 36 m s⁻¹ while a patrol car travelling along the same avenue travels directly away from the source at 22 m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) λ′ = (v + v_s) / f = 0.537 m. (b) v_rel = v − v_o = 318 m s⁻¹. (c) f′ = v_rel / λ′ = 592 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Computes shifted wavelength in air ahead of/behind moving source.
Combines wave speed v and observer speed v_o with correct relative sign.
Divides relative wave speed from (b) by wavelength from (a).

parts.prompt: Calculate the wavelength of the sound waves in the air between the source and the observer.
Determine the speed of these sound wavefronts relative to the moving observer.
Hence calculate the acoustic frequency detected by the observer.

items.stem: Coherent light of wavelength 420 nm from a violet semiconductor laser beam incident perpendicular to a dual-slit foil slide passes through slits of slit separation 0.35 mm onto a screen 3.4 m away. What is the linear distance on the screen from the central bright fringe (n = 0) to the n = 4 bright fringe?
items.workedSolution: Single fringe spacing = λD / d = 4.08 × 10⁻³ m. Distance from n = 0 to the n = 4 bright fringe is y_4 = 4 × λD / d = 0.0163 m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates single adjacent fringe spacing λD / d instead of multiplying by order n.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Applies destructive half-integer factor (n − ½) instead of constructive integer order n.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Fencepost error: multiplies fringe spacing by (n + 1) fringes instead of n intervals from n = 0.

items.stem: On a marine towing-tank wave maker, capacitance wire probes captures a displacement–position profile for monochromatic gravity waves along a channel of amplitude 0.03 m and wavelength 0.32 m propagating at 2.56 m s⁻¹. What is the frequency of oscillation of the wave?
items.workedSolution: Using f = v / λ with wave speed v = 2.56 m s⁻¹ and wavelength λ = 0.32 m gives f = 2.56 / 0.32 = 8.00 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Rearranges v = fλ to obtain f = v / λ = 8.00 Hz (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the oscillation period T = λ / v instead of the frequency f = v / λ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies wave speed by wavelength (vλ) instead of dividing v by λ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Mistakes two full cycles for one wavelength, halving the calculated frequency.

items.stem: Neglecting end corrections, an open-open anodised aluminium organ flue pipe in a recital hall of length 0.66 m contains air in which sound travels at 330 m s⁻¹. What is the frequency of its n = 5 standing-wave harmonic?
items.workedSolution: For an open pipe of length L = 0.66 m in harmonic n = 5, f_n = nv / (2L) = (5 × 330) / (2 × 0.66) = 1.25e+3 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes the fundamental frequency f₁ instead of the n-th harmonic.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses closed-one-end pipe relation nv / (4L) instead of open-both-ends nv / (2L).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in λ_n = 2L / n.

items.stem: Monochromatic light of wavelength 460 nm is incident normally on a physics Required Practical bench where a laser beam hits a clamped transmission grating squarely ruled with 400 lines mm⁻¹. Diffracted beams fall onto a flat observation screen placed 2.1 m behind and parallel to the grating, and measurements are taken for the n = 3 order.
items.workedSolution: (a) d = 10⁻³ / 400 = 2.50 × 10⁻⁶ m. (b) sin θ = nλ / d = 0.552, so θ = 33.5°. (c) On the flat screen, y = D tan θ = 2.1 × tan(33.5°) = 1.39 m.

markScheme.criterion: Recognises large-angle geometry y = D tan θ rather than small-angle D sin θ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the centre-to-centre spacing d between adjacent grating slits in metres.
Calculate the diffraction angle θ_3 (in degrees) of the order n = 3 maximum.
Determine the linear distance along the flat screen from the central maximum (n = 0) to the n = 3 maximum.
workingSteps: At large diffraction angles, use exact trigonometry y = D tan θ (do not assume tan θ ≈ sin θ).

items.stem: Along an ultrasonic non-destructive testing bench, elastic shear waves in a polymer bar of amplitude 0.022 m, wavelength 0.6 m, and frequency 25 Hz pass markers P at x₁ = 0.09 m and Q at x₂ = 0.48 m. What is the phase difference (in degrees) between P and Q?
items.workedSolution: Separation Δx = 0.48 m − 0.09 m = 0.39 m. Cycle span = 0.6 m, giving 0.650 cycles. Phase difference Δφ = 360° × 0.650 = 234°.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates fractional cycle separation and multiplies by 360° to get 234° (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes phase difference in radians without converting to degrees.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses half a cycle (180°) instead of a full cycle (360°) in the phase-difference formula.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the fractional cycle ratio (dividing cycle span by separation instead of separation by cycle span).

items.stem: Figure illustrates a quality-control laser diffractometer measuring beam spread through a narrow rectangular slit (width 0.08 mm) diffracting a normal-incidence beam of wavelength 514 nm onto a planar detector screen situated 1.8 m behind the aperture.
items.workedSolution: (a) θ = λ / b = 6.42 × 10⁻³ rad. (b) y₁ = θD = 0.0116 m. (c) Full central width w = 2y₁ = 0.0231 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies θ = λ / b in SI units.
Multiplies θ by screen distance D.
Doubles half-width to span both sides of the central peak.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular position θ (in radians) of the first diffraction minimum.
workingSteps: Use the small-angle single-slit first-minimum relation θ = λ / b.

parts.prompt: Determine the linear distance on the screen from the centre of the pattern to the first dark minimum.
Calculate the full linear width of the central bright maximum on the screen.
workingSteps: The central maximum spans from −y₁ to +y₁: w = 2y₁.

items.stem: During an optics experiment using an optical bench fitted with a Glan-Thompson calcite polarizer and a rotatable analyzer, a linearly polarized beam of intensity 84 W m⁻² strikes an ideal analyzer tilted at angle θ = 20° to the incident electric-field plane (transmitted intensity obeys I = I₀ cos²θ).
items.workedSolution: (a) E / E₀ = cos(20°) = 0.940. (b) I = I₀ cos²(20°) = 74.2 W m⁻². (c) Absorbed intensity = 84 − 74.2 = 9.83 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Projects electric-field vector via E / E₀ = cos θ.
Subtracts transmitted intensity from incident intensity.

parts.prompt: Calculate the ratio E / E₀ of the transmitted electric-field amplitude to the incident electric-field amplitude.
workingSteps: Only the electric-field component parallel to the analyzer axis is transmitted: E / E₀ = cos θ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the intensity I of the beam emerging from the analyzer.
Determine the intensity removed (absorbed or rejected) from the beam by the analyzer.

items.stem: Figure shows a quarter-wave automotive exhaust side-branch silencer closed at its far cap of length 0.42 m excited in odd harmonic n = 5 at 1036 Hz (end correction negligible). Calculate the speed of sound in the air column.
items.workedSolution: For a closed-one-end pipe in odd harmonic n = 5, λ_n = 4L / n = 4(0.42) / 5 = 0.336 m. Speed of sound v = f_n λ_n = 348 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v = 4Lf_n / n to obtain 348 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses open-pipe wavelength 2L / n instead of closed-pipe 4L / n, halving the speed of sound.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes an even harmonic index (n − 1) instead of the odd harmonic n.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Treats the n-th harmonic frequency as the fundamental mode v = 4Lf.

items.stem: During an outdoor acoustics trial (speed of sound in still air 332 m s⁻¹), a fire-appliance warning horn sounding continuously at 620 Hz recedes directly away from a pedestrian waiting at a kerbside crossing at 56 m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) Unshifted wavelength λ₀ = v / f = 0.535 m. (b) In the region towards the observer, λ′ = (v + v_s) / f = 0.626 m. (c) Observed frequency f′ = v / λ′ = 531 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Applies f′ = v / λ′ or exact moving-source Doppler formula.

parts.prompt: Calculate the wavelength that the sound waves would have in still air if the source were stationary.
Calculate the wavelength λ′ of the sound waves in the air between the moving source and the stationary observer.
Determine the frequency detected by the stationary observer.

items.stem: Figure illustrates a collimated green DPSS diode-pumped laser directed normally onto two narrow parallel slits illuminating slits with slit separation 0.36 mm at distance 2.4 m from a screen where the adjacent bright fringe spacing is 4.08 mm. Calculate the wavelength of the coherent beam.
items.workedSolution: Rearranging fringe spacing Δy = λD / d gives λ = Δy × d / D = (4.08 × 10⁻³ × 3.60 × 10⁻⁴) / 2.4 = 6.12 × 10⁻⁷ m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

markScheme.criterion: Rearranges double-slit relation to obtain λ = 6.12 × 10⁻⁷ m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Introduces a spurious factor of ½ from single-slit central-width formulas.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats bright-to-bright fringe spacing as half-wavelength path difference.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies fringe spacing by screen distance D and divides by slit separation instead of multiplying by slit separation / D.

items.stem: An unpolarized beam of unknown intensity I₀ passes sequentially through ideal polarizer P₁ and analyzer A (oriented at 35° to P₁) on a microwave horn link employing parallel wire-grid polarizing frames. If the final emerging intensity is 21.5 W m⁻² (where polarized transmission obeys I = I₁ cos²θ), what is the incident unpolarized intensity I₀?
items.workedSolution: Since I = ½ I₀ cos²θ, rearranging gives I₀ = 2I / cos²(35°) = (2 × 21.5) / 0.671 = 64.0 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Solves I = ½ I₀ cos²θ to obtain I₀ = 64.0 W m⁻² (D).

items.stem: In an acoustics experiment, a tungsten resonator filament clamped at both ends in a vacuum bell jar of vibrating length 0.64 m and mass per unit length 0.006 kg m⁻¹ is placed under a tension of 153.6 N and excited into its n = 5 harmonic mode. Transverse waves travel along a taut string of tension T and linear density μ at speed v = √(T / μ).

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T and μ into v = √(T / μ).
Divides wave speed from (a) by wavelength from (b).

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of transverse waves along the string.
Determine the wavelength of the n = 5 harmonic mode.
Calculate the resonant frequency of this standing wave.

items.stem: Figure depicts a discharge-lamp spectroscopy setup where collimated monochromatic light strikes a grating normally (450 lines mm⁻¹) illuminated squarely by coherent light of wavelength 575 nm. What total number of bright principal maxima can be detected on a semicircular detector track?
items.workedSolution: d = 10⁻³ / 450 = 2.22 × 10⁻⁶ m, so d / λ = 3.86 and n_max = 3. Including ±1..±3 and n = 0 gives 2(3) + 1 = 7 principal maxima.

items.stem: Figure depicts a sodium vapour discharge lamp filtered and collimated onto a Young's double-slit plate (wavelength 650 nm) illuminating a double-slit mask whose apertures each have width 0.06 mm and slit separation 0.18 mm, with an observation screen placed 1.4 m behind the mask.
items.workedSolution: (a) Interference fringe spacing Δy = λD / d = 5.06 × 10⁻³ m. (b) Central envelope full width w_env = 2λD / b = 0.0303 m. (c) First missing order n = d / b = 3.

markScheme.criterion: Uses λD / d with slit separation d.
Uses 2λD / b with individual slit width b.
Equates interference maximum angle to first diffraction minimum.

parts.prompt: Calculate the fringe spacing between adjacent double-slit interference maxima near the centre of the pattern.
Calculate the full width of the central single-slit diffraction envelope on the screen.
Determine the lowest positive interference order n that is missing due to coincidence with a single-slit diffraction minimum.
workingSteps: Equate nλ / d = λ / b => n = d / b.

items.stem: In a stationary-wave investigation, a cello A-string held taut between the fingerboard nut and tailpiece bridge of vibrating length 0.72 m is driven so that it resonates in its n = 5 harmonic mode, as shown. Transverse waves travel along the string at 252 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate the wavelength of this n = 5 harmonic standing wave.
workingSteps: For a string fixed at both ends, λ_n = 2L / n.

parts.prompt: Determine the oscillation frequency of this standing wave.
Calculate the fundamental (first-harmonic) frequency of the string when kept at the same tension.

items.stem: A stationary autonomous test-track vehicle ultrasonic-audible beacon radiates sound at 460 Hz in still air (speed of sound 343 m s⁻¹). Meanwhile, a second instrumented test vehicle on the straight lane travels directly away from the source and measures a frequency of 380 Hz. What is the speed of the moving observer?
items.workedSolution: For a stationary source and moving observer, f′ = f(v − v_o) / v. Rearranging gives v_o = v|f′ / f − 1| = 343 × |380 / 460 − 1| = 60.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses f′ = f(v ± v_o) / v to obtain v_o = 60.0 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: In an optics bench investigation with a cyan argon-ion laser beam passing through a pair of closely spaced parallel apertures, waves of wavelength 420 nm pass through a double slit of slit separation 0.55 mm onto a screen 3.4 m behind the barrier. A sensor records the n = 5 constructive maximum.
items.workedSolution: (a) Δℓ = nλ = 5 × 4.20 × 10⁻⁷ = 2.10 × 10⁻⁶ m. (b) θ_5 = arcsin(nλ / d) = 0.219°. (c) y_5 = nλD / d = 0.0130 m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

parts.prompt: Calculate the path difference between waves from S₁ and S₂ arriving at the n = 5 bright fringe.
workingSteps: For constructive interference at order n, Δℓ = nλ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deflection θ_5 (in degrees) of the n = 5 bright fringe from the central axis.
Determine the linear distance from the central bright fringe to the n = 5 bright fringe on the screen.

items.stem: Data from a sliding dipole probe on a microwavehorn bench receiver rail show a sinusoidal wave of amplitude 0.015 m and wavelength 0.6 m propagating rightwards at an oscillation frequency of 15 Hz.
items.workedSolution: (a) Period T = 1 / f = 1 / 15 = 0.0667 s. (b) Wave speed v = fλ = 15 × 0.6 = 9.00 m s⁻¹. (c) Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 94.2 rad s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = 1 / f with given frequency.
Substitutes into v = fλ or v = λ / T.

parts.prompt: Calculate the time period of oscillation of a point in the medium.
Determine the propagation speed of the progressive wave.
workingSteps: Apply v = fλ (or v = λ / T).

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular frequency ω of the wave oscillations.

items.stem: Figure shows a clear acrylic resonance tube held horizontally with both ends unobstructed of length 0.32 m sounding in stationary mode n = 3. Each open rim has an acoustic end correction of 0.02 m, and sound waves propagate at 340 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds twice the end correction: L_eff = L + 2e.

parts.prompt: Calculate the effective acoustic length L_eff between the two exterior antinodes.
workingSteps: An open-both-ends pipe has two open ends, so L_eff = L + 2e.

parts.prompt: Determine the wavelength of the n = 3 harmonic mode.
Calculate the resonant frequency of this standing wave.

items.stem: Monochromatic light of wavelength 460 nm strikes a physics Required Practical bench where a laser beam hits a clamped transmission grating squarely ruled with 400 lines mm⁻¹. At what angle θ from the normal is the order n = 3 principal maximum observed?
items.workedSolution: Grating spacing d = 10⁻³ / 400 = 2.50 × 10⁻⁶ m. Using d sin θ = nλ gives sin θ = (3 × 4.60 × 10⁻⁷) / 2.50 × 10⁻⁶ = 0.552, so θ = 33.5°.

markScheme.criterion: Converts d = 10⁻³ / N and solves d sin θ = nλ to get 33.5° (D).

items.stem: Using a coastal oceanography telemetry buoy array, an acoustic wave-height gauge captures a progressive wave in regular swell waves across a test basin with amplitude 0.022 m, wavelength 0.6 m, and frequency 4 Hz. Two particles P and Q along the propagation axis are located at x₁ = 0.15 m and x₂ = 0.375 m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the propagation speed of the wave.
Determine the oscillation period of particle P.
Calculate the phase difference, in radians, between the oscillations at P and Q.

items.stem: To calibrate a semiconductor-wafer metrology aperture illuminated squarely by a stabilised laser diode using a laser of wavelength 514 nm and screen distance 1.8 m, an engineer measures the full central diffraction maximum width to be 7.40 mm. Calculate the aperture width b.
items.workedSolution: Since full central maximum width w = 2λD / b, rearranging gives b = 2λD / w = (2 × 5.14 × 10⁻⁷ × 1.8) / 7.40 × 10⁻³ = 2.50 × 10⁻⁴ m.

markScheme.criterion: Rearranges w = 2λD / b to obtain b = 2.50 × 10⁻⁴ m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies λ by w and divides by 2D instead of computing b = 2λD / w.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in w = 2λD / b (treating full central width as λD / b), underestimating slit width by half.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 4λD / w instead of 2λD / w.

items.stem: To attenuate a plane-polarized beam from 32 W m⁻² down to 13.2 W m⁻² on a spectrophotometer polarization module with a precision rotary Vernier analyzer, an ideal analyzer is rotated through an acute angle θ from alignment (I = I₀ cos²θ). Determine θ.
items.workedSolution: From I = I₀ cos²θ, cos θ = √(13.2 / 32) = 0.643, giving θ = arccos(0.643) = 50.0°.

items.stem: During an acoustics practical, a Kundt's acoustic tube fitted with a rigid brass piston at one end and open at the other of length 0.85 m resonates in its n = 3 odd harmonic while sound travels at 336 m s⁻¹. Account for an end correction of 0.03 m beyond the single open end.
items.workedSolution: (a) L_eff = 0.880 m, giving f₁ = v / (4L_eff) = 95.5 Hz. (b) λ_3 = 4L_eff / 3 = 1.17 m. (c) f_3 = 3f₁ = 286 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Applies quarter-wave fundamental relation f₁ = v / (4L_eff).
Multiplies fundamental frequency by odd harmonic index 3 (or uses v / λ).

parts.prompt: Calculate the fundamental (first-harmonic, n = 1) frequency of this closed-end air column.
Determine the wavelength of the n = 3 harmonic standing wave.
Calculate the resonant frequency of this n = 3 harmonic mode.

items.stem: In still air where sound travels at 336 m s⁻¹, a high-speed sled mounted with an acoustic whistle sounds at 820 Hz while moving at 60 m s⁻¹ as it approaches directly towards a fixed microphone at the end of the test track. Which frequency is recorded?
items.workedSolution: For a source moving towards a stationary observer, f' = fv / (v − v_s) = (820 × 336) / (336 − 60) = 998 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Applies exact moving-source Doppler formula to obtain 998 Hz (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses the moving-observer formula AND reverses the sign of the Doppler frequency shift.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the Doppler sign in the denominator, using v + v_s for an approaching source (or v − v_s for a receding source).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Applies the moving-observer equation f(v ± v_s) / v instead of the moving-source equation fv / (v ∓ v_s).

items.stem: Monochromatic light of wavelength 488 nm from a blue gallium-nitride laser module aligned along an optical rail toward two parallel slits is incident normally on two narrow slits whose centre-to-centre slit separation is 0.45 mm. Interference fringes are observed on a flat screen placed 1.5 m from the slits.
items.workedSolution: (a) Fringe spacing = λD / d = (4.88 × 10⁻⁷ × 1.5) / 4.50 × 10⁻⁴ = 1.63 × 10⁻³ m. (b) First dark fringe distance = ½ × 1.63 × 10⁻³ = 8.13 × 10⁻⁴ m. (c) At order n = 2, path difference = nλ = 2 × 4.88 × 10⁻⁷ = 9.76 × 10⁻⁷ m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

markScheme.criterion: Converts units and substitutes into λD / (slit separation).
Takes half of the bright-fringe spacing.

parts.prompt: Calculate the fringe spacing between adjacent bright fringes on the screen.
Determine the distance on the screen from the central bright maximum to the centre of the first dark fringe.
workingSteps: First destructive minimum occurs halfway between the central and first-order bright maxima: y_dark,1 = 0.5 × fringe spacing.

parts.prompt: Calculate the geometric path difference between waves arriving from the two slits at the order n = 2 bright fringe.
workingSteps: Constructive interference at order n requires path difference Δℓ = nλ.

items.stem: An unpolarized beam of intensity 260 W m⁻² on a fibre-optics free-space polarization controller bench with an ideal linear analyzer passes normally through an ideal vertical polarizer P₁ and then through an ideal linear analyzer A whose transmission axis is rotated by θ = 70° from the vertical (for plane-polarized light of intensity I₁, analyzer transmission obeys I = I₁ cos²θ).
items.workedSolution: (a) After P₁, I₁ = ½ I₀ = 130 W m⁻². (b) After analyzer A, I = I₁ cos²(70°) = 15.2 W m⁻². (c) Overall fraction I / I₀ = ½ cos²(70°) = 0.0585.

markScheme.criterion: Halves unpolarized incident intensity at ideal polarizer P₁.
Applies I = I₁ cos²θ to the polarized beam.
Divides final transmitted intensity by incident unpolarized intensity I₀.

parts.prompt: State and calculate the intensity I₁ of the plane-polarized beam between polarizer P₁ and analyzer A.
workingSteps: Averaging cos²φ = ½ over all random polarization orientations reduces unpolarized intensity by half: I₁ = ½ I₀.

parts.prompt: Calculate the intensity I emerging from analyzer A.
workingSteps: Apply Malus's law I = I₁ cos²θ.

parts.prompt: Determine the overall fraction I / I₀ of the original unpolarized intensity transmitted by the two-filter combination.
workingSteps: Overall transmission fraction = I / I₀ = ½ cos²θ.

items.stem: Figure shows a sonometer constantan wire clamped rigidly between two knife-edge bridges of vibrating length 0.9 m and linear density 8 × 10⁻⁴ kg m⁻¹ tensioned at 7.22 N. Calculate the resonant frequency of harmonic mode n = 3.
items.workedSolution: Wave speed along the string is v = √(T / μ) = √(7.22 / 0.0008) = 95.0 m s⁻¹. For n = 3, f_n = nv / (2L) = 3 × 95.0 / (2 × 0.9) = 158 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates v = √(T / μ) and f_n = nv / (2L) = 158 Hz (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts tension and mass per unit length inside the radical, using √(μ / T).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in λ_n = 2L / n, computing (n / L)√(T / μ).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root over T / μ, computing (n / 2L)(T / μ).

items.stem: Figure shows monochromatic radiation of wavelength 580 nm incident normally on a transmission diffraction grating mounted on thevernier table of a spectrometer ruled at 300 lines mm⁻¹; an angular detector measures the n = 1 order and surveys all principal orders within ±90°.
items.workedSolution: (a) d = 3.33 × 10⁻⁶ m, so θ₁ = arcsin(λ / d) = 10.0°. (b) d / λ = 5.75, giving n_max = 5. (c) Total principal maxima = 2(5) + 1 = 11.

markScheme.criterion: Computes d = 10⁻³ / N and applies sin θ₁ = λ / d.
Evaluates d / λ = 5.75 and rounds down.

parts.prompt: Calculate the diffraction angle (in degrees) of the first-order (n = 1) maximum.
Determine the maximum observable diffraction order n_max for this wavelength.
workingSteps: Since sin θ ≤ 1, truncate down: n_max = floor(5.75) = 5.

parts.prompt: State the total number of bright principal maxima formed across the forward semicircle.

items.stem: Using a narrowband dye-laser beam striking a micro-machined silicon double-slit diaphragm of wavelength 650 nm at screen distance 2.6 m, two parallel slits each of individual slit width 0.08 mm are separated by centre-to-centre slit separation 0.32 mm. Which positive interference order n is the first missing order due to single-slit diffraction?
items.workedSolution: Interference maxima satisfy sin θ = nλ / d and the first single-slit minimum satisfies sin θ = λ / b. Dividing gives n = d / b = 3.20 × 10⁻⁴ / 8.00 × 10⁻⁵ = 4.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Selects the last bright interference order visible inside one side of the central envelope (d/b − 1) instead of the missing order d/b.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Counts the total number of bright fringes inside the central diffraction envelope (2d/b − 1) instead of the missing order index.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles d / b by using full angular width 2λ / b instead of first-minimum angle λ / b.

items.stem: On a steel acoustic-guitar treble string mounted between a nut and bridge saddle of length 0.96 m, transverse waves propagate at 168 m s⁻¹. What is the resonant frequency when the string vibrates in its n = 5 harmonic mode?
items.workedSolution: For a string fixed at both ends in harmonic n = 5, λ_n = 2L / n = 2(0.96) / 5 = 0.384 m. Thus f_n = v / λ_n = 168 / 0.384 = 438 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Applies f_n = nv / (2L) to obtain 438 Hz (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the first-harmonic fundamental frequency v / (2L) instead of multiplying by harmonic number n.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the closed-one-end pipe formula nv / (4L) instead of fixed-both-ends nv / (2L).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in λ_n = 2L / n, computing f = nv / L.

items.stem: Figure depicts an autonomous test-track vehicle ultrasonic-audible beacon (rest frequency 580 Hz) as it moves towards the observer at 28 m s⁻¹ along a straight line; at the same instant, a second instrumented test vehicle on the straight lane travels directly towards the source at 42 m s⁻¹ (speed of sound 340 m s⁻¹).
items.workedSolution: (a) λ′ = (v − v_s) / f = 0.538 m. (b) v_rel = v + v_o = 382 m s⁻¹. (c) f′ = v_rel / λ′ = 710 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Computes shifted wavelength in air ahead of/behind moving source.
Combines wave speed v and observer speed v_o with correct relative sign.
Divides relative wave speed from (b) by wavelength from (a).

parts.prompt: Calculate the wavelength of the sound waves in the air between the source and the observer.
Determine the speed of these sound wavefronts relative to the moving observer.
Hence calculate the acoustic frequency detected by the observer.

items.stem: Figure depicts a cyan argon-ion laser beam passing through a pair of closely spaced parallel apertures of wavelength 532 nm incident on slits with slit separation 0.22 mm and screen distance 3.4 m. How far from the central maximum does the order n = 4 bright fringe appear?
items.workedSolution: Single fringe spacing = λD / d = 8.22 × 10⁻³ m. Distance from n = 0 to the n = 4 bright fringe is y_4 = 4 × λD / d = 0.0329 m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates single adjacent fringe spacing λD / d instead of multiplying by order n.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Applies destructive half-integer factor (n − ½) instead of constructive integer order n.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Fencepost error: multiplies fringe spacing by (n + 1) fringes instead of n intervals from n = 0.

items.stem: Figure shows the spatial profile y(x) captured by an ultrasound line-scan for harmonic shear waves propagating through gel of wavelength 1.5 m and amplitude 0.036 m. Given a source frequency of 85 Hz, determine the wave speed.
items.workedSolution: From the displacement–position profile, wavelength λ = 1.5 m and frequency f = 85 Hz. Using the wave equation v = fλ = 85 Hz × 1.5 m = 128 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies v = fλ to obtain 128 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides wavelength by frequency (λ / f), confusing frequency f with period T.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides frequency by wavelength (f / λ) instead of applying v = fλ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the wavelength by misreading a two-cycle span as a single wavelength.

items.stem: Figure shows an open-open anodised aluminium organ flue pipe in a recital hall of length 0.52 m resonating in mode n = 1. Displacement antinodes form at an end correction e = 0.025 m beyond each open end, and sound travels at 340 m s⁻¹. Calculate the frequency of this harmonic.
items.workedSolution: Because the pipe is open at both ends, effective acoustic length L_eff = L + 2e = 0.52 + 2(0.025) = 0.570 m. For n = 1, λ_n = 2L_eff / n = 1.14 m, so f_n = v / λ_n = 340 / 1.14 = 298 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses the closed-pipe denominator 4L_eff instead of the open-pipe 2L_eff.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds only one end correction (L + e) instead of accounting for both open ends (L + 2e).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Ignores the acoustic end corrections completely, using physical length L instead of L + 2e.

items.stem: In an optical spectrometry setup, a student goniometer spectrometer carrying a ruled glass diffraction grating (200 lines mm⁻¹) is illuminated normally at wavelength 430 nm. A flat viewing screen sits 1.6 m downstream from the grating to record the order n = 3 principal maximum.
items.workedSolution: (a) d = 10⁻³ / 200 = 5.00 × 10⁻⁶ m. (b) sin θ = nλ / d = 0.258, so θ = 15.0°. (c) On the flat screen, y = D tan θ = 1.6 × tan(15.0°) = 0.427 m.

markScheme.criterion: Recognises large-angle geometry y = D tan θ rather than small-angle D sin θ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the centre-to-centre spacing d between adjacent grating slits in metres.
Calculate the diffraction angle θ_3 (in degrees) of the order n = 3 maximum.
Determine the linear distance along the flat screen from the central maximum (n = 0) to the n = 3 maximum.
workingSteps: At large diffraction angles, use exact trigonometry y = D tan θ (do not assume tan θ ≈ sin θ).

items.stem: A fixed detector on a taut rubber-cord wave demonstrator monitors sinusoidal disturbances driven by an eccentric cam of frequency 8 Hz, wavelength 1.2 m, and amplitude 0.022 m. Determine the phase change in radians between t = 0.01875 s (point P) and t = 0.1125 s (point Q).
items.workedSolution: Separation Δt = 0.1125 s − 0.01875 s = 0.09375 s. Cycle span = 1 / f = 0.125 s, giving 0.750 cycles. Phase difference Δφ = 2π × 0.750 = 4.71 rad.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates fractional cycle separation and multiplies by 2π rad to get 4.71 rad (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses half a cycle (π rad) instead of a full cycle (2π rad) in the phase-difference formula.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the fractional cycle ratio (dividing cycle span by separation instead of separation by cycle span).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes phase difference in degrees instead of radians.

items.stem: Figure illustrates an undergraduate optics rail setup projecting a single-slit Fraunhofer pattern onto a matte screen (width 0.18 mm) diffracting a normal-incidence beam of wavelength 405 nm onto a planar detector screen situated 1.8 m behind the aperture.
items.workedSolution: (a) θ = λ / b = 2.25 × 10⁻³ rad. (b) y₁ = θD = 4.05 × 10⁻³ m. (c) Full central width w = 2y₁ = 8.10 × 10⁻³ m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies θ = λ / b in SI units.
Multiplies θ by screen distance D.
Doubles half-width to span both sides of the central peak.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular position θ (in radians) of the first diffraction minimum.
workingSteps: Use the small-angle single-slit first-minimum relation θ = λ / b.

parts.prompt: Determine the linear distance on the screen from the centre of the pattern to the first dark minimum.
Calculate the full linear width of the central bright maximum on the screen.
workingSteps: The central maximum spans from −y₁ to +y₁: w = 2y₁.

items.stem: During an optics experiment using a photographic filter-transmission test bench with high-extinction linear polarizers, a linearly polarized beam of intensity 72 W m⁻² strikes an ideal analyzer tilted at angle θ = 35° to the incident electric-field plane (transmitted intensity obeys I = I₀ cos²θ).
items.workedSolution: (a) E / E₀ = cos(35°) = 0.819. (b) I = I₀ cos²(35°) = 48.3 W m⁻². (c) Absorbed intensity = 72 − 48.3 = 23.7 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Projects electric-field vector via E / E₀ = cos θ.
Subtracts transmitted intensity from incident intensity.

parts.prompt: Calculate the ratio E / E₀ of the transmitted electric-field amplitude to the incident electric-field amplitude.
workingSteps: Only the electric-field component parallel to the analyzer axis is transmitted: E / E₀ = cos θ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the intensity I of the beam emerging from the analyzer.
Determine the intensity removed (absorbed or rejected) from the beam by the analyzer.

items.stem: Inside a brass calibration air column sealed by an end-plug on the left and open on the right of physical length 0.52 m, the single open end has an antinode end correction of 0.018 m and sound travels at 336 m s⁻¹. What is the resonant frequency of the n = 7 harmonic?
items.workedSolution: Effective acoustic length for one closed and one open end is L_eff = L + e = 0.538 m. For odd harmonic n = 7, f_n = nv / (4L_eff) = (7 × 336) / (4 × 0.538) = 1.09e+3 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds end correction 2e as if both ends were open, rather than L + e for a single open end.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the open-end antinode correction e, using physical length L instead of L + e.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses open-pipe denominator 2(L + e) instead of closed-pipe 4(L + e).

items.stem: During an outdoor acoustics trial (speed of sound in still air 343 m s⁻¹), an express electric locomotive horn sounding continuously at 620 Hz approaches directly towards a commuter standing beside the straight track at 82 m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) Unshifted wavelength λ₀ = v / f = 0.553 m. (b) In the region towards the observer, λ′ = (v − v_s) / f = 0.421 m. (c) Observed frequency f′ = v / λ′ = 815 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Applies f′ = v / λ′ or exact moving-source Doppler formula.

parts.prompt: Calculate the wavelength that the sound waves would have in still air if the source were stationary.
Calculate the wavelength λ′ of the sound waves in the air between the moving source and the stationary observer.
Determine the frequency detected by the stationary observer.

items.stem: In an optics investigation with a violet semiconductor laser beam incident perpendicular to a dual-slit foil slide, light of wavelength 405 nm passes through two parallel slits of slit separation 0.5 mm onto a screen at distance 3.6 m. What is the fringe spacing between adjacent bright fringes on the screen?
items.workedSolution: Converting to SI units: λ = 4.05 × 10⁻⁷ m and slit separation = 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ m. Fringe spacing = λD / (slit separation) = (4.05 × 10⁻⁷ × 3.6) / 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ = 2.92 × 10⁻³ m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

markScheme.criterion: Uses fringe spacing = λD / (slit separation) to obtain 2.92 × 10⁻³ m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by slit separation and divides by screen distance (λd / D) instead of λD / d.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the distance from the central bright fringe to the first dark minimum (½ λD / d) instead of bright fringe spacing.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Includes an erroneous factor of 2, confusing double-slit fringe spacing with single-slit central maximum width.

items.stem: On a glare-suppression laboratory rig directing a collimated beam onto linear polarizing films, unpolarized light traverses ideal polarizer P₁ and analyzer A tilted at θ = 70° relative to P₁, yielding a transmitted intensity of 3.74 W m⁻² (I = I₁ cos²θ for plane-polarized light). Calculate the initial unpolarized intensity I₀.
items.workedSolution: Since I = ½ I₀ cos²θ, rearranging gives I₀ = 2I / cos²(70°) = (2 × 3.74) / 0.117 = 64.0 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Solves I = ½ I₀ cos²θ to obtain I₀ = 64.0 W m⁻² (D).

items.stem: Figure shows a laboratory vibration-generator wire clamped between bench G-clamps of length 1.1 m and linear mass density 0.0025 kg m⁻¹ held at tension 49 N while resonating in stationary harmonic n = 4 (transverse wave speed v = √(T / μ)).

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T and μ into v = √(T / μ).
Divides wave speed from (a) by wavelength from (b).

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of transverse waves along the string.
Determine the wavelength of the n = 4 harmonic mode.
Calculate the resonant frequency of this standing wave.

items.stem: A laser beam of wavelength 532 nm is incident normally on a holographic polymer grating slide illuminated at normal incidence on an optical rail with 500 lines mm⁻¹. Including the central zero-order beam, how many total principal maxima emerge across the forward semicircle (−90° ≤ θ ≤ +90°)?
items.workedSolution: d = 10⁻³ / 500 = 2.00 × 10⁻⁶ m, so d / λ = 3.76 and n_max = 3. Including ±1..±3 and n = 0 gives 2(3) + 1 = 7 principal maxima.

items.stem: Figure depicts a coherent laser source in a darkroom metrology rig illuminating two identical parallel slits (wavelength 514 nm) illuminating a double-slit mask whose apertures each have width 0.06 mm and slit separation 0.36 mm, with an observation screen placed 2.2 m behind the mask.
items.workedSolution: (a) Interference fringe spacing Δy = λD / d = 3.14 × 10⁻³ m. (b) Central envelope full width w_env = 2λD / b = 0.0377 m. (c) First missing order n = d / b = 6.

markScheme.criterion: Uses λD / d with slit separation d.
Uses 2λD / b with individual slit width b.
Equates interference maximum angle to first diffraction minimum.

parts.prompt: Calculate the fringe spacing between adjacent double-slit interference maxima near the centre of the pattern.
Calculate the full width of the central single-slit diffraction envelope on the screen.
Determine the lowest positive interference order n that is missing due to coincidence with a single-slit diffraction minimum.
workingSteps: Equate nλ / d = λ / b => n = d / b.

items.stem: A vibration generator excites an electric-bass nickel-wound string anchored between bridge and headstock nut of length 0.6 m into its 6th harmonic standing wave. The speed of transverse waves on the tensioned string is 72 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate the wavelength of this n = 6 harmonic standing wave.
workingSteps: For a string fixed at both ends, λ_n = 2L / n.

parts.prompt: Determine the oscillation frequency of this standing wave.
Calculate the fundamental (first-harmonic) frequency of the string when kept at the same tension.

items.stem: In still air where sound travels at 330 m s⁻¹, a fixed beacon (a fire-appliance warning horn) emits 700 Hz. As a patrol car travelling along the same avenue travels directly towards the source, its microphone detects 853 Hz. Determine the observer's speed.
items.workedSolution: For a stationary source and moving observer, f′ = f(v + v_o) / v. Rearranging gives v_o = v|f′ / f − 1| = 330 × |853 / 700 − 1| = 72.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses f′ = f(v ± v_o) / v to obtain v_o = 72.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.distractorRationale: Divides the speed by 2 as if solving a two-way pulse-echo Doppler shift.

options.distractorRationale: Applies the moving-source algebra v|1 − f / f'| instead of the moving-observer relation v|f' / f − 1|.

items.stem: Coherent plane waves of wavelength 660 nm from a stabilised monochromatic optical-bench laser incident at right angles on slits S₁ and S₂ strike a pair of slits whose slit separation is 0.35 mm, producing Young fringes on a screen 3.4 m downstream; consider the order n = 3 bright fringe.
items.workedSolution: (a) Δℓ = nλ = 3 × 6.60 × 10⁻⁷ = 1.98 × 10⁻⁶ m. (b) θ_3 = arcsin(nλ / d) = 0.324°. (c) y_3 = nλD / d = 0.0192 m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

parts.prompt: Calculate the path difference between waves from S₁ and S₂ arriving at the n = 3 bright fringe.
workingSteps: For constructive interference at order n, Δℓ = nλ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deflection θ_3 (in degrees) of the n = 3 bright fringe from the central axis.
Determine the linear distance from the central bright fringe to the n = 3 bright fringe on the screen.

items.stem: A continuous progressive wave in shallow water surface ripples is investigated on a ripple-tank stroboscope camera. Figure shows the spatial profile captured at a single instant, with amplitude 0.042 m and wavelength 0.48 m, driven continuously at 55 Hz.
items.workedSolution: (a) Period T = 1 / f = 1 / 55 = 0.0182 s. (b) Wave speed v = fλ = 55 × 0.48 = 26.4 m s⁻¹. (c) Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 346 rad s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = 1 / f with given frequency.
Substitutes into v = fλ or v = λ / T.

parts.prompt: Calculate the time period of oscillation of a point in the medium.
Determine the propagation speed of the progressive wave.
workingSteps: Apply v = fλ (or v = λ / T).

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular frequency ω of the wave oscillations.

items.stem: Figure shows a soprano recorder cylindrical bore section tested with both ends open of length 0.44 m sounding in stationary mode n = 3. Each open rim has an acoustic end correction of 0.025 m, and sound waves propagate at 340 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds twice the end correction: L_eff = L + 2e.

parts.prompt: Calculate the effective acoustic length L_eff between the two exterior antinodes.
workingSteps: An open-both-ends pipe has two open ends, so L_eff = L + 2e.

parts.prompt: Determine the wavelength of the n = 3 harmonic mode.
Calculate the resonant frequency of this standing wave.

items.stem: Monochromatic light of wavelength 514 nm strikes a telecommunications optical-spectrum test stage with a precision ruled grating ruled with 500 lines mm⁻¹. At what angle θ from the normal is the order n = 2 principal maximum observed?
items.workedSolution: Grating spacing d = 10⁻³ / 500 = 2.00 × 10⁻⁶ m. Using d sin θ = nλ gives sin θ = (2 × 5.14 × 10⁻⁷) / 2.00 × 10⁻⁶ = 0.514, so θ = 30.9°.

markScheme.criterion: Converts d = 10⁻³ / N and solves d sin θ = nλ to get 30.9° (D).

items.stem: A harmonic wave travelling through regular swell waves across a test basin is recorded on a coastal oceanography telemetry buoy array. The wave has amplitude 0.065 m, wavelength 1.6 m, and frequency 8 Hz; markers P and Q sit at equilibrium positions x₁ = 0.32 m and x₂ = 0.8 m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the propagation speed of the wave.
Determine the oscillation period of particle P.
Calculate the phase difference, in radians, between the oscillations at P and Q.

items.stem: To calibrate an optical-bench single-slit slide followed by a linear CCD photodiode screen using a laser of wavelength 589 nm and screen distance 2.5 m, an engineer measures the full central diffraction maximum width to be 29.4 mm. Calculate the aperture width b.
items.workedSolution: Since full central maximum width w = 2λD / b, rearranging gives b = 2λD / w = (2 × 5.89 × 10⁻⁷ × 2.5) / 0.0294 = 1.00 × 10⁻⁴ m.

markScheme.criterion: Rearranges w = 2λD / b to obtain b = 1.00 × 10⁻⁴ m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies λ by w and divides by 2D instead of computing b = 2λD / w.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in w = 2λD / b (treating full central width as λD / b), underestimating slit width by half.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 4λD / w instead of 2λD / w.

items.stem: On an optical-mineralogy bench testing transmission through crossed and angled polaroids, a vertically plane-polarized beam of intensity 84 W m⁻² is incident normally on an ideal linear analyzer whose transmission axis is rotated by 30° from the vertical. What is the transmitted intensity?
items.workedSolution: Because the incident beam is already plane-polarized, Malus's law gives I = I₀ cos²θ = 84 × cos²(30°) = 84 × 0.750 = 63.0 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Applies I = I₀ cos²(30°) = 63.0 W m⁻² (C).

items.stem: In a laboratory resonance experiment, a narrow quartz acoustic resonator closed at one termination and open at the opposite end has physical length 0.85 m, with an antinode end correction of 0.022 m at its single open rim. Sound waves travel through the air column at 348 m s⁻¹, and the column is excited in odd harmonic n = 5.
items.workedSolution: (a) L_eff = 0.872 m, giving f₁ = v / (4L_eff) = 99.8 Hz. (b) λ_5 = 4L_eff / 5 = 0.698 m. (c) f_5 = 5f₁ = 499 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Applies quarter-wave fundamental relation f₁ = v / (4L_eff).
Multiplies fundamental frequency by odd harmonic index 5 (or uses v / λ).

parts.prompt: Calculate the fundamental (first-harmonic, n = 1) frequency of this closed-end air column.
Determine the wavelength of the n = 5 harmonic standing wave.
Calculate the resonant frequency of this n = 5 harmonic mode.

items.stem: Emitting a continuous tone of frequency 750 Hz, a coastguard rescue-launch foghorn approaches directly towards a harbour-wall sound-level recorder at a constant speed of 76 m s⁻¹. Taking the speed of sound in still air as 343 m s⁻¹, what frequency is detected by the stationary observer?
items.workedSolution: For a source moving towards a stationary observer, f' = fv / (v − v_s) = (750 × 343) / (343 − 76) = 963 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Applies exact moving-source Doppler formula to obtain 963 Hz (D).

items.stem: Monochromatic light of wavelength 405 nm from a coherent laser source in a darkroom metrology rig illuminating two identical parallel slits is incident normally on two narrow slits whose centre-to-centre slit separation is 0.5 mm. Interference fringes are observed on a flat screen placed 1.2 m from the slits.
items.workedSolution: (a) Fringe spacing = λD / d = (4.05 × 10⁻⁷ × 1.2) / 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ = 9.72 × 10⁻⁴ m. (b) First dark fringe distance = ½ × 9.72 × 10⁻⁴ = 4.86 × 10⁻⁴ m. (c) At order n = 3, path difference = nλ = 3 × 4.05 × 10⁻⁷ = 1.22 × 10⁻⁶ m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

markScheme.criterion: Converts units and substitutes into λD / (slit separation).
Takes half of the bright-fringe spacing.

parts.prompt: Calculate the fringe spacing between adjacent bright fringes on the screen.
Determine the distance on the screen from the central bright maximum to the centre of the first dark fringe.
workingSteps: First destructive minimum occurs halfway between the central and first-order bright maxima: y_dark,1 = 0.5 × fringe spacing.

parts.prompt: Calculate the geometric path difference between waves arriving from the two slits at the order n = 3 bright fringe.
workingSteps: Constructive interference at order n requires path difference Δℓ = nλ.

items.stem: In a polarization experiment with a microwave horn link employing parallel wire-grid polarizing frames, unpolarized waves of intensity 96 W m⁻² strike ideal polarizer P₁ and subsequently pass through analyzer A oriented at angle θ = 20° to P₁ (for plane-polarized light, I = I₁ cos²θ).
items.workedSolution: (a) After P₁, I₁ = ½ I₀ = 48.0 W m⁻². (b) After analyzer A, I = I₁ cos²(20°) = 42.4 W m⁻². (c) Overall fraction I / I₀ = ½ cos²(20°) = 0.442.

markScheme.criterion: Halves unpolarized incident intensity at ideal polarizer P₁.
Applies I = I₁ cos²θ to the polarized beam.
Divides final transmitted intensity by incident unpolarized intensity I₀.

parts.prompt: State and calculate the intensity I₁ of the plane-polarized beam between polarizer P₁ and analyzer A.
workingSteps: Averaging cos²φ = ½ over all random polarization orientations reduces unpolarized intensity by half: I₁ = ½ I₀.

parts.prompt: Calculate the intensity I emerging from analyzer A.
workingSteps: Apply Malus's law I = I₁ cos²θ.

parts.prompt: Determine the overall fraction I / I₀ of the original unpolarized intensity transmitted by the two-filter combination.
workingSteps: Overall transmission fraction = I / I₀ = ½ cos²θ.

items.stem: An instrument maker adjusts the tension in an electric-bass nickel-wound string anchored between bridge and headstock nut of vibrating length 0.9 m and linear density 0.0032 kg m⁻¹ until harmonic mode n = 1 sounds at 69.44 Hz (wave speed v = √(T / μ)). Determine the string tension.
items.workedSolution: Wavelength λ_n = 2L / n = 2(0.9) / 1 = 1.80 m, so required wave speed v = f_n λ_n = 125 m s⁻¹. Rearranging v = √(T / μ) gives T = μv² = 0.0032 × (125)² = 50.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Finds v = 2Lf_n / n and computes T = μv² = 50.0 N (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Forgets to square the wave speed when rearranging v = √(T / μ) to T = μv².

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses λ_n = L / n instead of 2L / n, halving v and underestimating T = μv² by a factor of 4.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides v² by linear mass density μ instead of multiplying T = μv².

items.stem: Monochromatic plane waves of wavelength 575 nm illuminate a telecommunications optical-spectrum test stage with a precision ruled grating (450 lines mm⁻¹) normally, producing discrete diffraction orders beginning at n = 1 across the forward hemisphere.
items.workedSolution: (a) d = 2.22 × 10⁻⁶ m, so θ₁ = arcsin(λ / d) = 15.0°. (b) d / λ = 3.86, giving n_max = 3. (c) Total principal maxima = 2(3) + 1 = 7.

markScheme.criterion: Computes d = 10⁻³ / N and applies sin θ₁ = λ / d.
Evaluates d / λ = 3.86 and rounds down.

Determine the maximum observable diffraction order n_max for this wavelength.
workingSteps: Since sin θ ≤ 1, truncate down: n_max = floor(3.86) = 3.

parts.prompt: State the total number of bright principal maxima formed across the forward semicircle.

items.stem: Light of wavelength 650 nm from a helium-neon gas laser illuminating a precision photo-etched double slit illuminates a double slit of slit separation 0.4 mm in which each slit has finite width 0.08 mm. On a screen 1.4 m away, what is the full linear width of the central single-slit diffraction envelope?
items.workedSolution: The first single-slit diffraction minima lie at θ = ±λ / b, so the full width of the central diffraction envelope on the screen is w_env = 2λD / b = (2 × 6.50 × 10⁻⁷ × 1.4) / 8.00 × 10⁻⁵ = 0.0227 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses w_env = 2λD / b to obtain 0.0227 m (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes the adjacent interference fringe spacing λD / d instead of the diffraction envelope width 2λD / b.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes slit separation d in place of individual slit width b, computing 2λD / d.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the half-width λD / b from the centre to one minimum instead of the full width 2λD / b.

items.stem: Figure depicts a grand-piano phosphor-bronze bass wire anchored across its cast-iron frame of fixed length 1.2 m oscillating in harmonic n = 5. Given a transverse wave speed of 168 m s⁻¹, calculate the frequency of this stationary wave.
items.workedSolution: For a string fixed at both ends in harmonic n = 5, λ_n = 2L / n = 2(1.2) / 5 = 0.480 m. Thus f_n = v / λ_n = 168 / 0.480 = 350 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Applies f_n = nv / (2L) to obtain 350 Hz (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the first-harmonic fundamental frequency v / (2L) instead of multiplying by harmonic number n.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the closed-one-end pipe formula nv / (4L) instead of fixed-both-ends nv / (2L).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in λ_n = 2L / n, computing f = nv / L.

items.stem: During a straight-line Doppler measurement in still air (sound speed 340 m s⁻¹), an emergency ambulance siren sounding at 780 Hz moves towards the observer at 28 m s⁻¹ while a pursuit motorcycle carrying a calibrated microphone travels directly away from the source at 26 m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) λ′ = (v − v_s) / f = 0.400 m. (b) v_rel = v − v_o = 314 m s⁻¹. (c) f′ = v_rel / λ′ = 785 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Computes shifted wavelength in air ahead of/behind moving source.
Combines wave speed v and observer speed v_o with correct relative sign.
Divides relative wave speed from (b) by wavelength from (a).

parts.prompt: Calculate the wavelength of the sound waves in the air between the source and the observer.
Determine the speed of these sound wavefronts relative to the moving observer.
Hence calculate the acoustic frequency detected by the observer.

items.stem: When a stabilised monochromatic optical-bench laser incident at right angles on slits S₁ and S₂ of wavelength 532 nm illuminates two parallel slits at distance 1.4 m from a viewing screen, the distance from the central bright maximum to the n = 5 bright fringe is 8.87 mm. What is the slit separation?
items.workedSolution: Since y_n = nλD / d, slit separation d = nλD / y_n = (5 × 5.32 × 10⁻⁷ × 1.4) / 8.87 × 10⁻³ = 4.20 × 10⁻⁴ m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Treats the n-th bright fringe displacement as a single fringe spacing, omitting the factor of n.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Applies dark-fringe factor (n − ½) instead of integer n.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides total span by (n + 1) instead of n fringe intervals between n = 0 and order n.

items.stem: A progressive wave in shallow water surface ripples is monitored with a ripple-tank stroboscope camera. Its spatial snapshot shows amplitude 0.018 m and wavelength 0.32 m, and wavefronts advance at 2.56 m s⁻¹. Determine the source frequency.
items.workedSolution: Using f = v / λ with wave speed v = 2.56 m s⁻¹ and wavelength λ = 0.32 m gives f = 2.56 / 0.32 = 8.00 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Rearranges v = fλ to obtain f = v / λ = 8.00 Hz (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the oscillation period T = λ / v instead of the frequency f = v / λ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies wave speed by wavelength (vλ) instead of dividing v by λ.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Mistakes two full cycles for one wavelength, halving the calculated frequency.

items.stem: Neglecting end corrections, a soprano recorder cylindrical bore section tested with both ends open resonates in its n = 3 harmonic at 786.4 Hz when the speed of sound in air is 346 m s⁻¹. What is the physical length of the open pipe?
items.workedSolution: For an ideal pipe open at both ends, L = nv / (2f_n) = (3 × 346) / (2 × 786) = 0.660 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses L = nv / (2f_n) to obtain 0.660 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits harmonic number n, computing fundamental half-wavelength v / (2f_n).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Applies the closed-one-end pipe relation L = nv / (4f_n) instead of open-both-ends L = nv / (2f_n).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in L = nλ / 2.

items.stem: In an optical spectrometry setup, a student goniometer spectrometer carrying a ruled glass diffraction grating (200 lines mm⁻¹) is illuminated normally at wavelength 650 nm. A flat viewing screen sits 1.15 m downstream from the grating to record the order n = 3 principal maximum.
items.workedSolution: (a) d = 10⁻³ / 200 = 5.00 × 10⁻⁶ m. (b) sin θ = nλ / d = 0.390, so θ = 23.0°. (c) On the flat screen, y = D tan θ = 1.15 × tan(23.0°) = 0.487 m.

markScheme.criterion: Recognises large-angle geometry y = D tan θ rather than small-angle D sin θ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the centre-to-centre spacing d between adjacent grating slits in metres.
Calculate the diffraction angle θ_3 (in degrees) of the order n = 3 maximum.
Determine the linear distance along the flat screen from the central maximum (n = 0) to the n = 3 maximum.
workingSteps: At large diffraction angles, use exact trigonometry y = D tan θ (do not assume tan θ ≈ sin θ).

items.stem: Figure shows a snapshot from capacitance wire probes on a marine towing-tank wave maker for a wave of wavelength 2 m, frequency 50 Hz, and amplitude 0.035 m. Points P and Q lie at x₁ = 0.2 m and x₂ = 0.8 m. Calculate the phase difference in degrees between P and Q.
items.workedSolution: Separation Δx = 0.8 m − 0.2 m = 0.6 m. Cycle span = 2 m, giving 0.300 cycles. Phase difference Δφ = 360° × 0.300 = 108°.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates fractional cycle separation and multiplies by 360° to get 108° (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes phase difference in radians without converting to degrees.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses half a cycle (180°) instead of a full cycle (360°) in the phase-difference formula.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the fractional cycle ratio (dividing cycle span by separation instead of separation by cycle span).

items.stem: In an optics bench experiment, coherent light of wavelength 450 nm illuminates an undergraduate optics rail setup projecting a single-slit Fraunhofer pattern onto a matte screen of aperture width 0.25 mm, projecting a single-slit diffraction pattern onto a screen 3.5 m downstream.
items.workedSolution: (a) θ = λ / b = 1.80 × 10⁻³ rad. (b) y₁ = θD = 6.30 × 10⁻³ m. (c) Full central width w = 2y₁ = 0.0126 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies θ = λ / b in SI units.
Multiplies θ by screen distance D.
Doubles half-width to span both sides of the central peak.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular position θ (in radians) of the first diffraction minimum.
workingSteps: Use the small-angle single-slit first-minimum relation θ = λ / b.

parts.prompt: Determine the linear distance on the screen from the centre of the pattern to the first dark minimum.
Calculate the full linear width of the central bright maximum on the screen.
workingSteps: The central maximum spans from −y₁ to +y₁: w = 2y₁.

items.stem: On a glare-suppression laboratory rig directing a collimated beam onto linear polarizing films, a vertically plane-polarized beam of intensity 84 W m⁻² is incident normally on an ideal linear analyzer whose transmission axis makes an angle θ = 35° with the vertical (for plane-polarized light, Malus's law gives transmitted intensity I = I₀ cos²θ).
items.workedSolution: (a) E / E₀ = cos(35°) = 0.819. (b) I = I₀ cos²(35°) = 56.4 W m⁻². (c) Absorbed intensity = 84 − 56.4 = 27.6 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Projects electric-field vector via E / E₀ = cos θ.
Subtracts transmitted intensity from incident intensity.

parts.prompt: Calculate the ratio E / E₀ of the transmitted electric-field amplitude to the incident electric-field amplitude.
workingSteps: Only the electric-field component parallel to the analyzer axis is transmitted: E / E₀ = cos θ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the intensity I of the beam emerging from the analyzer.
Determine the intensity removed (absorbed or rejected) from the beam by the analyzer.

items.stem: Figure depicts a narrow quartz acoustic resonator closed at one termination and open at the opposite end of length 0.85 m resonating in the lowest-frequency overtone above its fundamental mode. Taking the speed of sound as 348 m s⁻¹ and ignoring end correction, calculate this resonant frequency.
items.workedSolution: A pipe closed at one end supports odd harmonics only (n = 1, 3, 5, ...), so the next resonant mode above the fundamental is n = 3. Thus f₃ = 3v / (4L) = 3(348) / (4 × 0.85) = 307 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies odd harmonic n = 3 and computes f₃ = 3v / (4L) = 307 Hz (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the fundamental (first-harmonic) frequency v / (4L) instead of the first overtone 3v / (4L).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Assumes an even n = 2 harmonic exists in a pipe closed at one end, computing 2f₁ = v / (2L) instead of 3f₁ = 3v / (4L).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the open-both-ends formula 3v / (2L) instead of closed-one-end 3v / (4L).

items.stem: During an outdoor acoustics trial (speed of sound in still air 340 m s⁻¹), an emergency ambulance siren sounding continuously at 560 Hz recedes directly away from a stationary roadside acoustic logger at 60 m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) Unshifted wavelength λ₀ = v / f = 0.607 m. (b) In the region towards the observer, λ′ = (v + v_s) / f = 0.714 m. (c) Observed frequency f′ = v / λ′ = 476 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Applies f′ = v / λ′ or exact moving-source Doppler formula.

Calculate the wavelength λ′ of the sound waves in the air between the moving source and the stationary observer.
Determine the frequency detected by the stationary observer.

items.stem: In an optics investigation with a coherent laser source in a darkroom metrology rig illuminating two identical parallel slits, light of wavelength 445 nm passes through two parallel slits of slit separation 0.36 mm onto a screen at distance 2.4 m. What is the fringe spacing between adjacent bright fringes on the screen?
items.workedSolution: Converting to SI units: λ = 4.45 × 10⁻⁷ m and slit separation = 3.60 × 10⁻⁴ m. Fringe spacing = λD / (slit separation) = (4.45 × 10⁻⁷ × 2.4) / 3.60 × 10⁻⁴ = 2.97 × 10⁻³ m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

markScheme.criterion: Uses fringe spacing = λD / (slit separation) to obtain 2.97 × 10⁻³ m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by slit separation and divides by screen distance (λd / D) instead of λD / d.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the distance from the central bright fringe to the first dark minimum (½ λD / d) instead of bright fringe spacing.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Includes an erroneous factor of 2, confusing double-slit fringe spacing with single-slit central maximum width.

items.stem: An unpolarized beam of unknown intensity I₀ passes sequentially through ideal polarizer P₁ and analyzer A (oriented at 70° to P₁) on a photographic filter-transmission test bench with high-extinction linear polarizers. If the final emerging intensity is 11.2 W m⁻² (where polarized transmission obeys I = I₁ cos²θ), what is the incident unpolarized intensity I₀?
items.workedSolution: Since I = ½ I₀ cos²θ, rearranging gives I₀ = 2I / cos²(70°) = (2 × 11.2) / 0.117 = 192 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Solves I = ½ I₀ cos²θ to obtain I₀ = 192 W m⁻² (D).

items.stem: In an acoustics experiment, a cello A-string held taut between the fingerboard nut and tailpiece bridge of vibrating length 1.1 m and mass per unit length 0.0015 kg m⁻¹ is placed under a tension of 18.15 N and excited into its n = 4 harmonic mode. Transverse waves travel along a taut string of tension T and linear density μ at speed v = √(T / μ).

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T and μ into v = √(T / μ).
Divides wave speed from (a) by wavelength from (b).

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of transverse waves along the string.
Determine the wavelength of the n = 4 harmonic mode.
Calculate the resonant frequency of this standing wave.

items.stem: A laser beam of wavelength 640 nm is incident normally on a discharge-lamp spectroscopy setup where collimated monochromatic light strikes a grating normally with 200 lines mm⁻¹. Including the central zero-order beam, how many total principal maxima emerge across the forward semicircle (−90° ≤ θ ≤ +90°)?
items.workedSolution: d = 10⁻³ / 200 = 5.00 × 10⁻⁶ m, so d / λ = 7.81 and n_max = 7. Including ±1..±7 and n = 0 gives 2(7) + 1 = 15 principal maxima.

items.stem: Figure depicts a stabilised monochromatic optical-bench laser incident at right angles on slits S₁ and S₂ (wavelength 488 nm) illuminating a double-slit mask whose apertures each have width 0.09 mm and slit separation 0.54 mm, with an observation screen placed 2.6 m behind the mask.
items.workedSolution: (a) Interference fringe spacing Δy = λD / d = 2.35 × 10⁻³ m. (b) Central envelope full width w_env = 2λD / b = 0.0282 m. (c) First missing order n = d / b = 6.

markScheme.criterion: Uses λD / d with slit separation d.
Uses 2λD / b with individual slit width b.
Equates interference maximum angle to first diffraction minimum.

parts.prompt: Calculate the fringe spacing between adjacent double-slit interference maxima near the centre of the pattern.
Calculate the full width of the central single-slit diffraction envelope on the screen.
Determine the lowest positive interference order n that is missing due to coincidence with a single-slit diffraction minimum.
workingSteps: Equate nλ / d = λ / b => n = d / b.

items.stem: A vibration generator excites an electric-bass nickel-wound string anchored between bridge and headstock nut of length 1.2 m into its 5th harmonic standing wave. The speed of transverse waves on the tensioned string is 192 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate the wavelength of this n = 5 harmonic standing wave.
workingSteps: For a string fixed at both ends, λ_n = 2L / n.

parts.prompt: Determine the oscillation frequency of this standing wave.
Calculate the fundamental (first-harmonic) frequency of the string when kept at the same tension.

items.stem: Figure shows an autonomous test-track vehicle ultrasonic-audible beacon (rest frequency 520 Hz) as it moves away from the observer at 45 m s⁻¹, while a second instrumented test vehicle on the straight lane travels directly away from the source at 30 m s⁻¹ through air where sound travels at 343 m s⁻¹. Calculate the observed frequency.

markScheme.criterion: Applies dual-motion Doppler equation to obtain 419 Hz (A).

items.stem: Using a stabilised monochromatic optical-bench laser incident at right angles on slits S₁ and S₂, coherent light of wavelength 560 nm illuminates two narrow parallel slits of slit separation 0.55 mm. An interference pattern is formed on a screen 3 m away, and a detector is positioned at the order n = 4 bright maximum.
items.workedSolution: (a) Δℓ = nλ = 4 × 5.60 × 10⁻⁷ = 2.24 × 10⁻⁶ m. (b) θ_4 = arcsin(nλ / d) = 0.233°. (c) y_4 = nλD / d = 0.0122 m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

parts.prompt: Calculate the path difference between waves from S₁ and S₂ arriving at the n = 4 bright fringe.
workingSteps: For constructive interference at order n, Δℓ = nλ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deflection θ_4 (in degrees) of the n = 4 bright fringe from the central axis.
Determine the linear distance from the central bright fringe to the n = 4 bright fringe on the screen.

items.stem: In an experiment using a physics laboratory slinky-spring track, a high-speed motion tracker records the instantaneous displacement–position profile y(x) of transverse harmonic pulses along the coil travelling to the left. The wave has amplitude 0.03 m, wavelength 0.48 m, and source frequency 55 Hz.
items.workedSolution: (a) Period T = 1 / f = 1 / 55 = 0.0182 s. (b) Wave speed v = fλ = 55 × 0.48 = 26.4 m s⁻¹. (c) Crest-to-trough distance = 2A = 0.0600 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = 1 / f with given frequency.
Substitutes into v = fλ or v = λ / T.

parts.prompt: Calculate the time period of oscillation of a point in the medium.
Determine the propagation speed of the progressive wave.
workingSteps: Apply v = fλ (or v = λ / T).

parts.prompt: Determine the total vertical distance moved by a medium particle in travelling from a wave crest to an adjacent trough.
workingSteps: Crest-to-trough vertical span equals twice the wave amplitude, Δy = 2A.

items.stem: An acoustic resonator consists of a cylindrical concert-flute body tube open to the atmosphere at both ends of physical length 0.36 m. When excited in its n = 1 harmonic mode, displacement antinodes form at an end correction e = 0.028 m beyond each open end. The speed of sound in the air column is 334 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds twice the end correction: L_eff = L + 2e.

parts.prompt: Calculate the effective acoustic length L_eff between the two exterior antinodes.
workingSteps: An open-both-ends pipe has two open ends, so L_eff = L + 2e.

parts.prompt: Determine the wavelength of the n = 1 harmonic mode.
Calculate the resonant frequency of this standing wave.

items.stem: On a transmission diffraction grating mounted on thevernier table of a spectrometer with 500 lines mm⁻¹, the order n = 3 diffraction maximum of a monochromatic beam is measured at θ = 57.1° from the straight-through direction. What is the wavelength of the light?
items.workedSolution: Slit spacing d = 10⁻³ / 500 = 2.00 × 10⁻⁶ m. Rearranging d sin θ = nλ gives λ = d sin(57.1°) / 3 = 5.60 × 10⁻⁷ m.

markScheme.criterion: Computes d = 10⁻³ / N and λ = d sin θ / n = 5.60 × 10⁻⁷ m (A).

items.stem: Using a coastal oceanography telemetry buoy array, an acoustic wave-height gauge captures a progressive wave in regular swell waves across a test basin with amplitude 0.028 m, wavelength 2 m, and frequency 25 Hz. Two particles P and Q along the propagation axis are located at x₁ = 0.3 m and x₂ = 0.6 m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the propagation speed of the wave.
Determine the oscillation period of particle P.
Calculate the phase difference, in radians, between the oscillations at P and Q.

items.stem: Monochromatic light of wavelength 488 nm passes through a darkroom diffraction bench where coherent plane waves pass through a single narrow aperture of slit width 0.1 mm onto a screen 2.2 m away. What is the full linear width of the central bright diffraction maximum on the screen?
items.workedSolution: First diffraction minima lie at θ = ±λ / b, giving half-width y₁ = λD / b = 0.0107 m. Full central maximum width w = 2λD / b = 0.0215 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses w = 2λD / b to obtain 0.0215 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by slit width b and divides by screen distance D instead of 2λD / b.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates λD / b (the distance from the centre to one first-order minimum) instead of the full central maximum width 2λD / b.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by 4 instead of 2 when doubling the first-minimum half-width.

items.stem: Figure shows plane-polarized light of intensity 24 W m⁻² entering an ideal analyzer set at an angle of 20° to the incident electric-field plane on a stress-photoelasticity polariscope bench with graduated rotary analyzer mount. Calculate the emerging beam intensity.
items.workedSolution: Because the incident beam is already plane-polarized, Malus's law gives I = I₀ cos²θ = 24 × cos²(20°) = 24 × 0.883 = 21.2 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Applies I = I₀ cos²(20°) = 21.2 W m⁻² (C).

options.label: D

items.stem: An acoustic column consists of a pan-flute bamboo cane sealed by a natural node at the bottom and open at the top of length 0.24 m (end correction negligible) filled with air in which sound travels at 348 m s⁻¹. The air column resonates in its n = 7 odd harmonic mode, as shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) L_eff = 0.240 m, giving f₁ = v / (4L_eff) = 363 Hz. (b) λ_7 = 4L_eff / 7 = 0.137 m. (c) f_7 = 7f₁ = 2.54e+3 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Applies quarter-wave fundamental relation f₁ = v / (4L_eff).
Multiplies fundamental frequency by odd harmonic index 7 (or uses v / λ).

parts.prompt: Calculate the fundamental (first-harmonic, n = 1) frequency of this closed-end air column.
workingSteps: For a pipe closed at one end, λ₁ = 4L so f₁ = v / (4L).

parts.prompt: Determine the wavelength of the n = 7 harmonic standing wave.
Calculate the resonant frequency of this n = 7 harmonic mode.

items.stem: In still air where sound travels at 336 m s⁻¹, a racing telemetry drone emitting a steady acoustic tone sounds at 620 Hz while moving at 82 m s⁻¹ as it approaches directly towards a trackside timing marshal. Which frequency is recorded?
items.workedSolution: For a source moving towards a stationary observer, f' = fv / (v − v_s) = (620 × 336) / (336 − 82) = 820 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Applies exact moving-source Doppler formula to obtain 820 Hz (D).

options.distractorRationale: Uses the moving-observer formula AND reverses the sign of the Doppler frequency shift.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the Doppler sign in the denominator, using v + v_s for an approaching source (or v − v_s for a receding source).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Applies the moving-observer equation f(v ± v_s) / v instead of the moving-source equation fv / (v ∓ v_s).

items.stem: In a darkroom optics experiment, a violet semiconductor laser beam incident perpendicular to a dual-slit foil slide emits coherent light of wavelength 445 nm onto a double slit of slit separation 0.45 mm, with an observation screen positioned 1.5 m away.
items.workedSolution: (a) Fringe spacing = λD / d = (4.45 × 10⁻⁷ × 1.5) / 4.50 × 10⁻⁴ = 1.48 × 10⁻³ m. (b) First dark fringe distance = ½ × 1.48 × 10⁻³ = 7.42 × 10⁻⁴ m. (c) At order n = 2, path difference = nλ = 2 × 4.45 × 10⁻⁷ = 8.90 × 10⁻⁷ m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

markScheme.criterion: Converts units and substitutes into λD / (slit separation).
Takes half of the bright-fringe spacing.

parts.prompt: Calculate the fringe spacing between adjacent bright fringes on the screen.
Determine the distance on the screen from the central bright maximum to the centre of the first dark fringe.
workingSteps: First destructive minimum occurs halfway between the central and first-order bright maxima: y_dark,1 = 0.5 × fringe spacing.

parts.prompt: Calculate the geometric path difference between waves arriving from the two slits at the order n = 2 bright fringe.
workingSteps: Constructive interference at order n requires path difference Δℓ = nλ.

items.stem: An unpolarized beam of intensity 220 W m⁻² on a liquid-crystal display (LCD) backlight test rig using thin-film linear polaroid sheets passes normally through an ideal vertical polarizer P₁ and then through an ideal linear analyzer A whose transmission axis is rotated by θ = 20° from the vertical (for plane-polarized light of intensity I₁, analyzer transmission obeys I = I₁ cos²θ).
items.workedSolution: (a) After P₁, I₁ = ½ I₀ = 110 W m⁻². (b) After analyzer A, I = I₁ cos²(20°) = 97.1 W m⁻². (c) Overall fraction I / I₀ = ½ cos²(20°) = 0.442.

markScheme.criterion: Halves unpolarized incident intensity at ideal polarizer P₁.
Applies I = I₁ cos²θ to the polarized beam.
Divides final transmitted intensity by incident unpolarized intensity I₀.

parts.prompt: State and calculate the intensity I₁ of the plane-polarized beam between polarizer P₁ and analyzer A.
workingSteps: Averaging cos²φ = ½ over all random polarization orientations reduces unpolarized intensity by half: I₁ = ½ I₀.

parts.prompt: Calculate the intensity I emerging from analyzer A.
workingSteps: Apply Malus's law I = I₁ cos²θ.

parts.prompt: Determine the overall fraction I / I₀ of the original unpolarized intensity transmitted by the two-filter combination.
workingSteps: Overall transmission fraction = I / I₀ = ½ cos²θ.

items.stem: Figure shows a laboratory vibration-generator wire clamped between bench G-clamps (length 0.9 m, mass per unit length 0.0012 kg m⁻¹) vibrating in harmonic n = 3 at 208.3 Hz. Using v = √(T / μ), calculate the tension applied to the string.
items.workedSolution: Wavelength λ_n = 2L / n = 2(0.9) / 3 = 0.600 m, so required wave speed v = f_n λ_n = 125 m s⁻¹. Rearranging v = √(T / μ) gives T = μv² = 0.0012 × (125)² = 18.8 N.

markScheme.criterion: Finds v = 2Lf_n / n and computes T = μv² = 18.8 N (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Forgets to square the wave speed when rearranging v = √(T / μ) to T = μv².

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses λ_n = L / n instead of 2L / n, halving v and underestimating T = μv² by a factor of 4.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides v² by linear mass density μ instead of multiplying T = μv².

items.stem: A collimated beam of wavelength 532 nm strikes a collimated laser wavelength-calibration rig fitted with a plane transmission grating ruled with 500 lines mm⁻¹ at normal incidence. Diffracted maxima are scanned across the full forward semicircle (−90° < θ < +90°), starting with the first-order (n = 1) beam.
items.workedSolution: (a) d = 2.00 × 10⁻⁶ m, so θ₁ = arcsin(λ / d) = 15.4°. (b) d / λ = 3.76, giving n_max = 3. (c) Total principal maxima = 2(3) + 1 = 7.

markScheme.criterion: Computes d = 10⁻³ / N and applies sin θ₁ = λ / d.
Evaluates d / λ = 3.76 and rounds down.
