parts.prompt: Calculate the diffraction angle (in degrees) of the first-order (n = 1) maximum.
Determine the maximum observable diffraction order n_max for this wavelength.
workingSteps: Since sin θ ≤ 1, truncate down: n_max = floor(3.76) = 3.

parts.prompt: State the total number of bright principal maxima formed across the forward semicircle.

items.stem: Coherent light of wavelength 450 nm from a helium-neon gas laser illuminating a precision photo-etched double slit strikes a double slit of slit separation 0.3 mm placed 2.6 m from a screen. If the first diffraction-envelope minimum suppresses the n = 4 interference maximum, determine each slit's width b.
items.workedSolution: The first single-slit minimum occurs at θ = λ / b while the n-th double-slit maximum is at θ = nλ / d. Coincidence at n = 4 gives b = d / 4 = 3.00 × 10⁻⁴ / 4 = 7.50 × 10⁻⁵ m.

markScheme.criterion: Equates λ / b = nλ / d to obtain b = d / 4 = 7.50 × 10⁻⁵ m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides slit separation by (n + 1) instead of missing order n = d / b.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the highest visible order inside the central envelope (n − 1) instead of the missing order n.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Includes an erroneous factor of 2 from the full angular width of the central envelope.

items.stem: Figure shows a cello A-string held taut between the fingerboard nut and tailpiece bridge of length 0.6 m vibrating in stationary harmonic mode n = 3 (wave speed 192 m s⁻¹). Determine the separation between consecutive nodes along the string.
items.workedSolution: In the n = 3 harmonic on a fixed string of length L = 0.6 m, n half-wavelength loops fit along L, so adjacent node spacing d_NN = λ / 2 = L / n = 0.6 / 3 = 0.200 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses d_NN = λ / 2 = L / n to obtain 0.200 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the node-to-adjacent-antinode distance λ / 4 instead of adjacent node spacing λ / 2.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides string length L by the total number of nodes (n + 1) instead of the number of loops n.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates a full wavelength λ = 2L / n instead of the half-wavelength node-to-node spacing λ / 2.

items.stem: In calm air where acoustic waves travel at 336 m s⁻¹, an autonomous test-track vehicle ultrasonic-audible beacon radiates a continuous 860 Hz tone as it moves away from the observer at 32 m s⁻¹, while a second instrumented test vehicle on the straight lane travels directly towards the source at 30 m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) λ′ = (v + v_s) / f = 0.428 m. (b) v_rel = v + v_o = 366 m s⁻¹. (c) f′ = v_rel / λ′ = 855 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Computes shifted wavelength in air ahead of/behind moving source.
Combines wave speed v and observer speed v_o with correct relative sign.
Divides relative wave speed from (b) by wavelength from (a).

parts.prompt: Calculate the wavelength of the sound waves in the air between the source and the observer.
Determine the speed of these sound wavefronts relative to the moving observer.
Hence calculate the acoustic frequency detected by the observer.

items.stem: Figure depicts a cyan argon-ion laser beam passing through a pair of closely spaced parallel apertures of wavelength 488 nm incident on slits with slit separation 0.28 mm and screen distance 1.4 m. How far from the central maximum does the order n = 5 bright fringe appear?
items.workedSolution: Single fringe spacing = λD / d = 2.44 × 10⁻³ m. Distance from n = 0 to the n = 5 bright fringe is y_5 = 5 × λD / d = 0.0122 m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates single adjacent fringe spacing λD / d instead of multiplying by order n.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Applies destructive half-integer factor (n − ½) instead of constructive integer order n.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Fencepost error: multiplies fringe spacing by (n + 1) fringes instead of n intervals from n = 0.

items.stem: Measurements from capacitance wire probes on a marine towing-tank wave maker show a sinusoidal wave of amplitude 0.018 m and wavelength 1.2 m travelling leftwards at a speed of 6 m s⁻¹. Which value gives the wave frequency?
items.workedSolution: Using f = v / λ with wave speed v = 6 m s⁻¹ and wavelength λ = 1.2 m gives f = 6 / 1.2 = 5.00 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Rearranges v = fλ to obtain f = v / λ = 5.00 Hz (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the oscillation period T = λ / v instead of the frequency f = v / λ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Mistakes two full cycles for one wavelength, halving the calculated frequency.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies wave speed by wavelength (vλ) instead of dividing v by λ.

items.stem: Figure illustrates a clear acrylic resonance tube held horizontally with both ends unobstructed of length 0.9 m vibrating in harmonic mode n = 5 when the speed of sound is 330 m s⁻¹ (end correction negligible). Calculate the frequency emitted.
items.workedSolution: For an open pipe of length L = 0.9 m in harmonic n = 5, f_n = nv / (2L) = (5 × 330) / (2 × 0.9) = 917 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes the fundamental frequency f₁ instead of the n-th harmonic.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses closed-one-end pipe relation nv / (4L) instead of open-both-ends nv / (2L).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in λ_n = 2L / n.

items.stem: Figure shows a normal-incidence beam of wavelength 430 nm diffracted by an astronomical spectrograph test bench using a normal-incidence transmission grating having 600 lines mm⁻¹ onto a planar screen 0.85 m away; consider the n = 1 bright order.
items.workedSolution: (a) d = 10⁻³ / 600 = 1.67 × 10⁻⁶ m. (b) sin θ = nλ / d = 0.258, so θ = 15.0°. (c) On the flat screen, y = D tan θ = 0.85 × tan(15.0°) = 0.227 m.

markScheme.criterion: Recognises large-angle geometry y = D tan θ rather than small-angle D sin θ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the centre-to-centre spacing d between adjacent grating slits in metres.
Calculate the diffraction angle θ_1 (in degrees) of the order n = 1 maximum.
Determine the linear distance along the flat screen from the central maximum (n = 0) to the n = 1 maximum.
workingSteps: At large diffraction angles, use exact trigonometry y = D tan θ (do not assume tan θ ≈ sin θ).

items.stem: Along a geotechnical seismic array, horizontally polarized surface waves in bedrock of amplitude 0.022 m, wavelength 0.36 m, and frequency 25 Hz pass markers P at x₁ = 0.072 m and Q at x₂ = 0.306 m. What is the phase difference (in degrees) between P and Q?
items.workedSolution: Separation Δx = 0.306 m − 0.072 m = 0.234 m. Cycle span = 0.36 m, giving 0.650 cycles. Phase difference Δφ = 360° × 0.650 = 234°.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates fractional cycle separation and multiplies by 360° to get 234° (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes phase difference in radians without converting to degrees.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses half a cycle (180°) instead of a full cycle (360°) in the phase-difference formula.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the fractional cycle ratio (dividing cycle span by separation instead of separation by cycle span).

items.stem: In an optics bench experiment, coherent light of wavelength 650 nm illuminates a darkroom diffraction bench where coherent plane waves pass through a single narrow aperture of aperture width 0.08 mm, projecting a single-slit diffraction pattern onto a screen 1.8 m downstream.
items.workedSolution: (a) θ = λ / b = 8.13 × 10⁻³ rad. (b) y₁ = θD = 0.0146 m. (c) Full central width w = 2y₁ = 0.0293 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies θ = λ / b in SI units.
Multiplies θ by screen distance D.
Doubles half-width to span both sides of the central peak.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular position θ (in radians) of the first diffraction minimum.
workingSteps: Use the small-angle single-slit first-minimum relation θ = λ / b.

parts.prompt: Determine the linear distance on the screen from the centre of the pattern to the first dark minimum.
Calculate the full linear width of the central bright maximum on the screen.
workingSteps: The central maximum spans from −y₁ to +y₁: w = 2y₁.

items.stem: On a photographic filter-transmission test bench with high-extinction linear polarizers, a vertically plane-polarized beam of intensity 240 W m⁻² is incident normally on an ideal linear analyzer whose transmission axis makes an angle θ = 30° with the vertical (for plane-polarized light, Malus's law gives transmitted intensity I = I₀ cos²θ).
items.workedSolution: (a) E / E₀ = cos(30°) = 0.866. (b) I = I₀ cos²(30°) = 180 W m⁻². (c) Absorbed intensity = 240 − 180 = 60.0 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Projects electric-field vector via E / E₀ = cos θ.
Subtracts transmitted intensity from incident intensity.

parts.prompt: Calculate the ratio E / E₀ of the transmitted electric-field amplitude to the incident electric-field amplitude.
workingSteps: Only the electric-field component parallel to the analyzer axis is transmitted: E / E₀ = cos θ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the intensity I of the beam emerging from the analyzer.
Determine the intensity removed (absorbed or rejected) from the beam by the analyzer.

items.stem: Neglecting end corrections, a narrow quartz acoustic resonator closed at one termination and open at the opposite end of length 0.24 m is excited from its fundamental mode up to the very next resonant standing-wave mode (first overtone), as shown. If the speed of sound is 336 m s⁻¹, what is this resonant frequency?
items.workedSolution: A pipe closed at one end supports odd harmonics only (n = 1, 3, 5, ...), so the next resonant mode above the fundamental is n = 3. Thus f₃ = 3v / (4L) = 3(336) / (4 × 0.24) = 1.05e+3 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies odd harmonic n = 3 and computes f₃ = 3v / (4L) = 1.05e+3 Hz (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the fundamental (first-harmonic) frequency v / (4L) instead of the first overtone 3v / (4L).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Assumes an even n = 2 harmonic exists in a pipe closed at one end, computing 2f₁ = v / (2L) instead of 3f₁ = 3v / (4L).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the open-both-ends formula 3v / (2L) instead of closed-one-end 3v / (4L).

items.stem: Sound waves propagate at 343 m s⁻¹ through calm air while a high-speed sled mounted with an acoustic whistle, emitting a steady 680 Hz signal, approaches directly towards a fixed microphone at the end of the test track at speed 56 m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) Unshifted wavelength λ₀ = v / f = 0.504 m. (b) In the region towards the observer, λ′ = (v − v_s) / f = 0.422 m. (c) Observed frequency f′ = v / λ′ = 813 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Applies f′ = v / λ′ or exact moving-source Doppler formula.

parts.prompt: Calculate the wavelength that the sound waves would have in still air if the source were stationary.
Calculate the wavelength λ′ of the sound waves in the air between the moving source and the stationary observer.
Determine the frequency detected by the stationary observer.

items.stem: Figure shows a stabilised monochromatic optical-bench laser incident at right angles on slits S₁ and S₂ of wavelength 589 nm illuminating slits separated by a slit separation of 0.24 mm. An observation screen is placed 1.5 m away. Calculate the centre-to-centre fringe spacing of the interference maxima.
items.workedSolution: Converting to SI units: λ = 5.89 × 10⁻⁷ m and slit separation = 2.40 × 10⁻⁴ m. Fringe spacing = λD / (slit separation) = (5.89 × 10⁻⁷ × 1.5) / 2.40 × 10⁻⁴ = 3.68 × 10⁻³ m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

markScheme.criterion: Uses fringe spacing = λD / (slit separation) to obtain 3.68 × 10⁻³ m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by slit separation and divides by screen distance (λd / D) instead of λD / d.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the distance from the central bright fringe to the first dark minimum (½ λD / d) instead of bright fringe spacing.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Includes an erroneous factor of 2, confusing double-slit fringe spacing with single-slit central maximum width.

items.stem: In a two-filter test on an optical bench fitted with a Glan-Thompson calcite polarizer and a rotatable analyzer, an unpolarized beam of intensity 36 W m⁻² traverses ideal polarizer P₁ followed by analyzer A angled at 65° to P₁'s axis (I = I₁ cos²θ for plane-polarized light). Determine the emerging intensity.
items.workedSolution: Ideal polarizer P₁ transmits half of the unpolarized intensity: I₁ = ½ I₀ = 18.0 W m⁻². Analyzer A then transmits I = I₁ cos²(65°) = ½(36) cos²(65°) = 3.21 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Applies I = ½ I₀ cos²(65°) = 3.21 W m⁻² (A).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses ½ I₀ sin²θ (complement angle) instead of ½ I₀ cos²θ.

items.stem: Figure shows a steel acoustic-guitar treble string mounted between a nut and bridge saddle of length 1.1 m and linear mass density 0.0025 kg m⁻¹ held at tension 110.3 N while resonating in stationary harmonic n = 4 (transverse wave speed v = √(T / μ)).

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T and μ into v = √(T / μ).
Divides wave speed from (a) by wavelength from (b).

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of transverse waves along the string.
Determine the wavelength of the n = 4 harmonic mode.
Calculate the resonant frequency of this standing wave.

items.stem: When a laser beam of wavelength 545 nm hits a darkroom laser diffractometer holding a multi-slit transmission grating perpendicular to the beam having 480 lines mm⁻¹ squarely, what is the largest integer order n for which a principal maximum is formed?
items.workedSolution: Grating spacing d = 10⁻³ / 480 = 2.08 × 10⁻⁶ m. Since sin θ ≤ 1, n ≤ d / λ = 2.08 × 10⁻⁶ / 5.45 × 10⁻⁷ = 3.82. Taking the floor gives n_max = 3.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates d / λ = 3.82 and takes floor to get n_max = 3 (A).

items.stem: A parallel beam of wavelength 633 nm from a stabilised monochromatic optical-bench laser incident at right angles on slits S₁ and S₂ strikes two slits of finite aperture width 0.075 mm and slit separation 0.3 mm; the resulting single-slit-modulated interference fringes are recorded 2.6 m downstream.
items.workedSolution: (a) Interference fringe spacing Δy = λD / d = 5.49 × 10⁻³ m. (b) Central envelope full width w_env = 2λD / b = 0.0439 m. (c) First missing order n = d / b = 4.

markScheme.criterion: Uses λD / d with slit separation d.
Uses 2λD / b with individual slit width b.
Equates interference maximum angle to first diffraction minimum.

parts.prompt: Calculate the fringe spacing between adjacent double-slit interference maxima near the centre of the pattern.
Calculate the full width of the central single-slit diffraction envelope on the screen.
Determine the lowest positive interference order n that is missing due to coincidence with a single-slit diffraction minimum.
workingSteps: Equate nλ / d = λ / b => n = d / b.

items.stem: A vibration generator excites a grand-piano phosphor-bronze bass wire anchored across its cast-iron frame of length 0.84 m into its 4th harmonic standing wave. The speed of transverse waves on the tensioned string is 192 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate the wavelength of this n = 4 harmonic standing wave.
workingSteps: For a string fixed at both ends, λ_n = 2L / n.

parts.prompt: Determine the oscillation frequency of this standing wave.
Calculate the fundamental (first-harmonic) frequency of the string when kept at the same tension.

items.stem: Figure shows an express electric locomotive horn (rest frequency 700 Hz) as it moves towards the observer at 40 m s⁻¹, while an inspection trolley rolling along the parallel rail travels directly towards the source at 26 m s⁻¹ through air where sound travels at 343 m s⁻¹. Calculate the observed frequency.

markScheme.criterion: Applies dual-motion Doppler equation to obtain 852 Hz (D).

items.stem: Coherent plane waves of wavelength 460 nm from a blue gallium-nitride laser module aligned along an optical rail toward two parallel slits strike a pair of slits whose slit separation is 0.28 mm, producing Young fringes on a screen 1.4 m downstream; consider the order n = 5 bright fringe.
items.workedSolution: (a) Δℓ = nλ = 5 × 4.60 × 10⁻⁷ = 2.30 × 10⁻⁶ m. (b) θ_5 = arcsin(nλ / d) = 0.471°. (c) y_5 = nλD / d = 0.0115 m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

parts.prompt: Calculate the path difference between waves from S₁ and S₂ arriving at the n = 5 bright fringe.
workingSteps: For constructive interference at order n, Δℓ = nλ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deflection θ_5 (in degrees) of the n = 5 bright fringe from the central axis.
Determine the linear distance from the central bright fringe to the n = 5 bright fringe on the screen.

items.stem: A continuous progressive wave in continuous electromagnetic waves in air is investigated on a microwavehorn bench receiver rail. Figure shows the spatial profile captured at a single instant, with amplitude 0.075 m and wavelength 0.32 m, driven continuously at 15 Hz.
items.workedSolution: (a) Period T = 1 / f = 1 / 15 = 0.0667 s. (b) Wave speed v = fλ = 15 × 0.32 = 4.80 m s⁻¹. (c) Crest-to-trough distance = 2A = 0.150 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = 1 / f with given frequency.
Substitutes into v = fλ or v = λ / T.

parts.prompt: Calculate the time period of oscillation of a point in the medium.
Determine the propagation speed of the progressive wave.
workingSteps: Apply v = fλ (or v = λ / T).

parts.prompt: Determine the total vertical distance moved by a medium particle in travelling from a wave crest to an adjacent trough.
workingSteps: Crest-to-trough vertical span equals twice the wave amplitude, Δy = 2A.

items.stem: An acoustic resonator consists of a copper HVAC acoustic resonator duct open at each termination of physical length 0.36 m. When excited in its n = 2 harmonic mode, displacement antinodes form at an end correction e = 0.018 m beyond each open end. The speed of sound in the air column is 330 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds twice the end correction: L_eff = L + 2e.

parts.prompt: Calculate the effective acoustic length L_eff between the two exterior antinodes.
workingSteps: An open-both-ends pipe has two open ends, so L_eff = L + 2e.

parts.prompt: Determine the wavelength of the n = 2 harmonic mode.
Calculate the resonant frequency of this standing wave.

items.stem: On a metrology optical encoder bench illuminating a ruled glass grating at zero angle of incidence with 500 lines mm⁻¹, the order n = 2 diffraction maximum of a monochromatic beam is measured at θ = 36.1° from the straight-through direction. What is the wavelength of the light?
items.workedSolution: Slit spacing d = 10⁻³ / 500 = 2.00 × 10⁻⁶ m. Rearranging d sin θ = nλ gives λ = d sin(36.1°) / 2 = 5.89 × 10⁻⁷ m.

markScheme.criterion: Computes d = 10⁻³ / N and λ = d sin θ / n = 5.89 × 10⁻⁷ m (A).

items.stem: A harmonic wave travelling through travelling pressure-displacement waves in nitrogen is recorded on an acoustic impedance-tube transducer rig. The wave has amplitude 0.045 m, wavelength 1.2 m, and frequency 4 Hz; markers P and Q sit at equilibrium positions x₁ = 0.3 m and x₂ = 0.72 m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the propagation speed of the wave.
Determine the oscillation period of particle P.
Calculate the phase difference, in radians, between the oscillations at P and Q.

items.stem: In an optical-bench single-slit slide followed by a linear CCD photodiode screen, coherent light of wavelength 670 nm forms a Fraunhofer pattern on a screen 2.5 m behind the aperture. If the full width of the central bright maximum between its first dark minima is 22.3 mm, what is the slit width b?
items.workedSolution: Since full central maximum width w = 2λD / b, rearranging gives b = 2λD / w = (2 × 6.70 × 10⁻⁷ × 2.5) / 0.0223 = 1.50 × 10⁻⁴ m.

markScheme.criterion: Rearranges w = 2λD / b to obtain b = 1.50 × 10⁻⁴ m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies λ by w and divides by 2D instead of computing b = 2λD / w.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in w = 2λD / b (treating full central width as λD / b), underestimating slit width by half.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 4λD / w instead of 2λD / w.

items.stem: During a calibration on a fibre-optics free-space polarization controller bench with an ideal linear analyzer, plane-polarized radiation of intensity 240 W m⁻² strikes an analyzer tilted at θ = 35° relative to the incident polarization axis. Determine the transmitted intensity.
items.workedSolution: Because the incident beam is already plane-polarized, Malus's law gives I = I₀ cos²θ = 240 × cos²(35°) = 240 × 0.671 = 161 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Applies I = I₀ cos²(35°) = 161 W m⁻² (C).

items.stem: An acoustic column consists of a quarter-wave automotive exhaust side-branch silencer closed at its far cap of length 0.28 m (end correction negligible) filled with air in which sound travels at 340 m s⁻¹. The air column resonates in its n = 3 odd harmonic mode, as shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) L_eff = 0.280 m, giving f₁ = v / (4L_eff) = 304 Hz. (b) λ_3 = 4L_eff / 3 = 0.373 m. (c) f_3 = 3f₁ = 911 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Applies quarter-wave fundamental relation f₁ = v / (4L_eff).
Multiplies fundamental frequency by odd harmonic index 3 (or uses v / λ).

parts.prompt: Calculate the fundamental (first-harmonic, n = 1) frequency of this closed-end air column.
workingSteps: For a pipe closed at one end, λ₁ = 4L so f₁ = v / (4L).

parts.prompt: Determine the wavelength of the n = 3 harmonic standing wave.
Calculate the resonant frequency of this n = 3 harmonic mode.

items.stem: Sounding continuously at 820 Hz, an express electric locomotive horn approaches directly towards a commuter standing beside the straight track through still air (speed of sound 340 m s⁻¹). If the stationary observer records a shifted frequency of 1.11e+3 Hz, what is the speed of the source?
items.workedSolution: Rearranging f' = fv / (v − v_s) gives v − v_s = vf / f' = (340 × 820) / 1.11e+3, yielding v_s = 88.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves f' = fv / (v ∓ v_s) for v_s = 88.0 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Halves the source speed as if applying a two-way radar reflection formula.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the low-speed / moving-observer relation v|f'/f − 1| instead of rearranging the exact moving-source formula f' = fv / (v ∓ v_s).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Stops at the effective denominator speed v(f / f') without taking the difference from v.

items.stem: Monochromatic light of wavelength 405 nm from a violet semiconductor laser beam incident perpendicular to a dual-slit foil slide is incident normally on two narrow slits whose centre-to-centre slit separation is 0.16 mm. Interference fringes are observed on a flat screen placed 1.8 m from the slits.
items.workedSolution: (a) Fringe spacing = λD / d = (4.05 × 10⁻⁷ × 1.8) / 1.60 × 10⁻⁴ = 4.56 × 10⁻³ m. (b) First dark fringe distance = ½ × 4.56 × 10⁻³ = 2.28 × 10⁻³ m. (c) At order n = 3, path difference = nλ = 3 × 4.05 × 10⁻⁷ = 1.22 × 10⁻⁶ m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

markScheme.criterion: Converts units and substitutes into λD / (slit separation).
Takes half of the bright-fringe spacing.

parts.prompt: Calculate the fringe spacing between adjacent bright fringes on the screen.
Determine the distance on the screen from the central bright maximum to the centre of the first dark fringe.
workingSteps: First destructive minimum occurs halfway between the central and first-order bright maxima: y_dark,1 = 0.5 × fringe spacing.

parts.prompt: Calculate the geometric path difference between waves arriving from the two slits at the order n = 3 bright fringe.
workingSteps: Constructive interference at order n requires path difference Δℓ = nλ.

items.stem: Figure shows unpolarized radiation of intensity 192 W m⁻² entering a liquid-crystal display (LCD) backlight test rig using thin-film linear polaroid sheets, traversing ideal vertical polarizer P₁ followed by linear analyzer An inclined at θ = 70° relative to P₁ (Malus's law for polarized light: I = I₁ cos²θ).
items.workedSolution: (a) After P₁, I₁ = ½ I₀ = 96.0 W m⁻². (b) After analyzer A, I = I₁ cos²(70°) = 11.2 W m⁻². (c) Overall fraction I / I₀ = ½ cos²(70°) = 0.0585.

markScheme.criterion: Halves unpolarized incident intensity at ideal polarizer P₁.
Applies I = I₁ cos²θ to the polarized beam.
Divides final transmitted intensity by incident unpolarized intensity I₀.

parts.prompt: State and calculate the intensity I₁ of the plane-polarized beam between polarizer P₁ and analyzer A.
workingSteps: Averaging cos²φ = ½ over all random polarization orientations reduces unpolarized intensity by half: I₁ = ½ I₀.

parts.prompt: Calculate the intensity I emerging from analyzer A.
workingSteps: Apply Malus's law I = I₁ cos²θ.

parts.prompt: Determine the overall fraction I / I₀ of the original unpolarized intensity transmitted by the two-filter combination.
workingSteps: Overall transmission fraction = I / I₀ = ½ cos²θ.

items.stem: To tune a steel acoustic-guitar treble string mounted between a nut and bridge saddle of length 0.64 m and linear mass density 0.0015 kg m⁻¹, its n = 1 harmonic must resonate at 164.1 Hz. Given that transverse wave speed on a taut string is v = √(T / μ), what tension T is required?
items.workedSolution: Wavelength λ_n = 2L / n = 2(0.64) / 1 = 1.28 m, so required wave speed v = f_n λ_n = 210 m s⁻¹. Rearranging v = √(T / μ) gives T = μv² = 0.0015 × (210)² = 66.2 N.

markScheme.criterion: Finds v = 2Lf_n / n and computes T = μv² = 66.2 N (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Forgets to square the wave speed when rearranging v = √(T / μ) to T = μv².

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses λ_n = L / n instead of 2L / n, halving v and underestimating T = μv² by a factor of 4.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides v² by linear mass density μ instead of multiplying T = μv².

items.stem: A collimated beam of wavelength 590 nm strikes a transmission diffraction grating mounted on thevernier table of a spectrometer ruled with 600 lines mm⁻¹ at normal incidence. Diffracted maxima are scanned across the full forward semicircle (−90° < θ < +90°), starting with the first-order (n = 1) beam.
items.workedSolution: (a) d = 1.67 × 10⁻⁶ m, so θ₁ = arcsin(λ / d) = 20.7°. (b) d / λ = 2.82, giving n_max = 2. (c) Total principal maxima = 2(2) + 1 = 5.

markScheme.criterion: Computes d = 10⁻³ / N and applies sin θ₁ = λ / d.
Evaluates d / λ = 2.82 and rounds down.

parts.prompt: Calculate the diffraction angle (in degrees) of the first-order (n = 1) maximum.
Determine the maximum observable diffraction order n_max for this wavelength.
workingSteps: Since sin θ ≤ 1, truncate down: n_max = floor(2.82) = 2.

parts.prompt: State the total number of bright principal maxima formed across the forward semicircle.

items.stem: In a helium-neon gas laser illuminating a precision photo-etched double slit (wavelength 450 nm, screen distance 1.4 m), two slits have centre-to-centre slit separation 0.45 mm. Single-slit diffraction modulates the pattern so that the n = 6 interference order is the lowest positive missing order. What is the width b of each individual slit?
items.workedSolution: The first single-slit minimum occurs at θ = λ / b while the n-th double-slit maximum is at θ = nλ / d. Coincidence at n = 6 gives b = d / 6 = 4.50 × 10⁻⁴ / 6 = 7.50 × 10⁻⁵ m.

markScheme.criterion: Equates λ / b = nλ / d to obtain b = d / 6 = 7.50 × 10⁻⁵ m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides slit separation by (n + 1) instead of missing order n = d / b.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the highest visible order inside the central envelope (n − 1) instead of the missing order n.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Includes an erroneous factor of 2 from the full angular width of the central envelope.

items.stem: Figure shows a tungsten resonator filament clamped at both ends in a vacuum bell jar of length 0.72 m vibrating in stationary harmonic mode n = 3 (wave speed 126 m s⁻¹). Determine the separation between consecutive nodes along the string.
items.workedSolution: In the n = 3 harmonic on a fixed string of length L = 0.72 m, n half-wavelength loops fit along L, so adjacent node spacing d_NN = λ / 2 = L / n = 0.72 / 3 = 0.240 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses d_NN = λ / 2 = L / n to obtain 0.240 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the node-to-adjacent-antinode distance λ / 4 instead of adjacent node spacing λ / 2.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides string length L by the total number of nodes (n + 1) instead of the number of loops n.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates a full wavelength λ = 2L / n instead of the half-wavelength node-to-node spacing λ / 2.

items.stem: In calm air where acoustic waves travel at 340 m s⁻¹, an aerobatic prop-plane acoustic beacon radiates a continuous 400 Hz tone as it moves away from the observer at 36 m s⁻¹, while a runway calibration vehicle travels directly away from the source at 42 m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) λ′ = (v + v_s) / f = 0.940 m. (b) v_rel = v − v_o = 298 m s⁻¹. (c) f′ = v_rel / λ′ = 317 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Computes shifted wavelength in air ahead of/behind moving source.
Combines wave speed v and observer speed v_o with correct relative sign.
Divides relative wave speed from (b) by wavelength from (a).

parts.prompt: Calculate the wavelength of the sound waves in the air between the source and the observer.
Determine the speed of these sound wavefronts relative to the moving observer.
Hence calculate the acoustic frequency detected by the observer.

items.stem: When a sodium vapour discharge lamp filtered and collimated onto a Young's double-slit plate of wavelength 488 nm illuminates two parallel slits at distance 1.75 m from a viewing screen, the distance from the central bright maximum to the n = 4 bright fringe is 8.13 mm. What is the slit separation?
items.workedSolution: Since y_n = nλD / d, slit separation d = nλD / y_n = (4 × 4.88 × 10⁻⁷ × 1.75) / 8.13 × 10⁻³ = 4.20 × 10⁻⁴ m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Treats the n-th bright fringe displacement as a single fringe spacing, omitting the factor of n.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Applies dark-fringe factor (n − ½) instead of integer n.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides total span by (n + 1) instead of n fringe intervals between n = 0 and order n.

items.stem: On a dielectric waveguide bench, a crystal detector carriage captures a displacement–position profile for guided millimetre-wave oscillations of amplitude 0.048 m and wavelength 0.75 m propagating at 26.25 m s⁻¹. What is the frequency of oscillation of the wave?
items.workedSolution: Using f = v / λ with wave speed v = 26.25 m s⁻¹ and wavelength λ = 0.75 m gives f = 26.25 / 0.75 = 35.0 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Rearranges v = fλ to obtain f = v / λ = 35.0 Hz (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the oscillation period T = λ / v instead of the frequency f = v / λ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Mistakes two full cycles for one wavelength, halving the calculated frequency.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies wave speed by wavelength (vλ) instead of dividing v by λ.

items.stem: Figure shows an orchestral piccolo cylindrical test bore open at both extremities of length 0.44 m resonating in mode n = 4. Displacement antinodes form at an end correction e = 0.028 m beyond each open end, and sound travels at 343 m s⁻¹. Calculate the frequency of this harmonic.
items.workedSolution: Because the pipe is open at both ends, effective acoustic length L_eff = L + 2e = 0.44 + 2(0.028) = 0.496 m. For n = 4, λ_n = 2L_eff / n = 0.248 m, so f_n = v / λ_n = 343 / 0.248 = 1.38e+3 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses the closed-pipe denominator 4L_eff instead of the open-pipe 2L_eff.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds only one end correction (L + e) instead of accounting for both open ends (L + 2e).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Ignores the acoustic end corrections completely, using physical length L instead of L + 2e.

items.stem: Coherent radiation of wavelength 532 nm strikes a student goniometer spectrometer carrying a ruled glass diffraction grating (200 lines mm⁻¹) perpendicularly, projecting discrete diffraction orders onto a flat screen at distance 1.15 m, where a sensor tracks the n = 3 maximum.
items.workedSolution: (a) d = 10⁻³ / 200 = 5.00 × 10⁻⁶ m. (b) sin θ = nλ / d = 0.319, so θ = 18.6°. (c) On the flat screen, y = D tan θ = 1.15 × tan(18.6°) = 0.387 m.

markScheme.criterion: Recognises large-angle geometry y = D tan θ rather than small-angle D sin θ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the centre-to-centre spacing d between adjacent grating slits in metres.
Calculate the diffraction angle θ_3 (in degrees) of the order n = 3 maximum.
Determine the linear distance along the flat screen from the central maximum (n = 0) to the n = 3 maximum.
workingSteps: At large diffraction angles, use exact trigonometry y = D tan θ (do not assume tan θ ≈ sin θ).

items.stem: On a coastal oceanography telemetry buoy array, an acoustic wave-height gauge records a displacement–time wave trace of amplitude 0.014 m, wavelength 0.8 m, and frequency 8 Hz. Two instants P and Q occur at t₁ = 0.025 s and t₂ = 0.0625 s. What is the phase difference (in radians) between instants P and Q?
items.workedSolution: Separation Δt = 0.0625 s − 0.025 s = 0.0375 s. Cycle span = 1 / f = 0.125 s, giving 0.300 cycles. Phase difference Δφ = 2π × 0.300 = 1.88 rad.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates fractional cycle separation and multiplies by 2π rad to get 1.88 rad (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses half a cycle (π rad) instead of a full cycle (2π rad) in the phase-difference formula.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the fractional cycle ratio (dividing cycle span by separation instead of separation by cycle span).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes phase difference in degrees instead of radians.

items.stem: A laser beam of wavelength 650 nm strikes a darkroom diffraction bench where coherent plane waves pass through a single narrow aperture whose slit width is 0.12 mm; a photodiode array placed 3 m away records the central maximum and flanking minima.
items.workedSolution: (a) θ = λ / b = 5.42 × 10⁻³ rad. (b) y₁ = θD = 0.0163 m. (c) Full central width w = 2y₁ = 0.0325 m.

markScheme.criterion: Applies θ = λ / b in SI units.
Multiplies θ by screen distance D.
Doubles half-width to span both sides of the central peak.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular position θ (in radians) of the first diffraction minimum.
workingSteps: Use the small-angle single-slit first-minimum relation θ = λ / b.

parts.prompt: Determine the linear distance on the screen from the centre of the pattern to the first dark minimum.
Calculate the full linear width of the central bright maximum on the screen.
workingSteps: The central maximum spans from −y₁ to +y₁: w = 2y₁.

items.stem: On a microwave horn link employing parallel wire-grid polarizing frames, a vertically plane-polarized beam of intensity 32 W m⁻² is incident normally on an ideal linear analyzer whose transmission axis makes an angle θ = 25° with the vertical (for plane-polarized light, Malus's law gives transmitted intensity I = I₀ cos²θ).
items.workedSolution: (a) E / E₀ = cos(25°) = 0.906. (b) I = I₀ cos²(25°) = 26.3 W m⁻². (c) Absorbed intensity = 32 − 26.3 = 5.72 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Projects electric-field vector via E / E₀ = cos θ.
Subtracts transmitted intensity from incident intensity.

parts.prompt: Calculate the ratio E / E₀ of the transmitted electric-field amplitude to the incident electric-field amplitude.
workingSteps: Only the electric-field component parallel to the analyzer axis is transmitted: E / E₀ = cos θ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the intensity I of the beam emerging from the analyzer.
Determine the intensity removed (absorbed or rejected) from the beam by the analyzer.

items.stem: Figure shows a brass calibration air column sealed by an end-plug on the left and open on the right (length 0.85 m, single open-end correction e = 0.026 m) resonating in odd harmonic n = 3 with sound speed 330 m s⁻¹. Calculate this resonant frequency.
items.workedSolution: Effective acoustic length for one closed and one open end is L_eff = L + e = 0.876 m. For odd harmonic n = 3, f_n = nv / (4L_eff) = (3 × 330) / (4 × 0.876) = 283 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Adds end correction 2e as if both ends were open, rather than L + e for a single open end.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the open-end antinode correction e, using physical length L instead of L + e.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses open-pipe denominator 2(L + e) instead of closed-pipe 4(L + e).

items.stem: In still air where the speed of sound is 332 m s⁻¹, an autonomous test-track vehicle ultrasonic-audible beacon emits sound of constant frequency 820 Hz while it recedes directly away from a fixed acoustic array post at a steady speed of 56 m s⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) Unshifted wavelength λ₀ = v / f = 0.405 m. (b) In the region towards the observer, λ′ = (v + v_s) / f = 0.473 m. (c) Observed frequency f′ = v / λ′ = 702 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Applies f′ = v / λ′ or exact moving-source Doppler formula.

parts.prompt: Calculate the wavelength that the sound waves would have in still air if the source were stationary.
Calculate the wavelength λ′ of the sound waves in the air between the moving source and the stationary observer.
Determine the frequency detected by the stationary observer.

items.stem: Figure shows a blue gallium-nitride laser module aligned along an optical rail toward two parallel slits of wavelength 650 nm illuminating slits separated by a slit separation of 0.6 mm. An observation screen is placed 2.4 m away. Calculate the centre-to-centre fringe spacing of the interference maxima.
items.workedSolution: Converting to SI units: λ = 6.50 × 10⁻⁷ m and slit separation = 6.00 × 10⁻⁴ m. Fringe spacing = λD / (slit separation) = (6.50 × 10⁻⁷ × 2.4) / 6.00 × 10⁻⁴ = 2.60 × 10⁻³ m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

markScheme.criterion: Uses fringe spacing = λD / (slit separation) to obtain 2.60 × 10⁻³ m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by slit separation and divides by screen distance (λd / D) instead of λD / d.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the distance from the central bright fringe to the first dark minimum (½ λD / d) instead of bright fringe spacing.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Includes an erroneous factor of 2, confusing double-slit fringe spacing with single-slit central maximum width.

items.stem: In a two-filter test on a spectrophotometer polarization module with a precision rotary Vernier analyzer, an unpolarized beam of intensity 36 W m⁻² traverses ideal polarizer P₁ followed by analyzer A angled at 50° to P₁'s axis (I = I₁ cos²θ for plane-polarized light). Determine the emerging intensity.
items.workedSolution: Ideal polarizer P₁ transmits half of the unpolarized intensity: I₁ = ½ I₀ = 18.0 W m⁻². Analyzer A then transmits I = I₁ cos²(50°) = ½(36) cos²(50°) = 7.44 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Applies I = ½ I₀ cos²(50°) = 7.44 W m⁻² (A).

items.stem: In an acoustics experiment, a grand-piano phosphor-bronze bass wire anchored across its cast-iron frame of vibrating length 0.5 m and mass per unit length 0.0012 kg m⁻¹ is placed under a tension of 8.67 N and excited into its n = 1 harmonic mode. Transverse waves travel along a taut string of tension T and linear density μ at speed v = √(T / μ).

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T and μ into v = √(T / μ).
Divides wave speed from (a) by wavelength from (b).

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of transverse waves along the string.
Determine the wavelength of the n = 1 harmonic mode.
Calculate the resonant frequency of this standing wave.

items.stem: Figure shows a physics Required Practical bench where a laser beam hits a clamped transmission grating squarely (250 lines mm⁻¹) illuminated perpendicularly by monochromatic light of wavelength 680 nm. Determine the maximum observable order n_max.
items.workedSolution: Grating spacing d = 10⁻³ / 250 = 4.00 × 10⁻⁶ m. Since sin θ ≤ 1, n ≤ d / λ = 4.00 × 10⁻⁶ / 6.80 × 10⁻⁷ = 5.88. Taking the floor gives n_max = 5.

items.stem: Monochromatic light of wavelength 488 nm from a narrowband dye-laser beam striking a micro-machined silicon double-slit diaphragm passes normally through two parallel slits of centre-to-centre slit separation 0.3 mm, where each slit has finite width 0.06 mm. The modulated interference pattern is projected onto a screen 3.2 m away.
items.workedSolution: (a) Interference fringe spacing Δy = λD / d = 5.21 × 10⁻³ m. (b) Central envelope full width w_env = 2λD / b = 0.0521 m. (c) First missing order n = d / b = 5.

markScheme.criterion: Uses λD / d with slit separation d.
Uses 2λD / b with individual slit width b.
Equates interference maximum angle to first diffraction minimum.

parts.prompt: Calculate the fringe spacing between adjacent double-slit interference maxima near the centre of the pattern.
Calculate the full width of the central single-slit diffraction envelope on the screen.
Determine the lowest positive interference order n that is missing due to coincidence with a single-slit diffraction minimum.
workingSteps: Equate nλ / d = λ / b => n = d / b.

items.stem: A vibration generator excites an electromagnetically driven Melde's apparatus cord fixed at both supports of length 0.96 m into its 4th harmonic standing wave. The speed of transverse waves on the tensioned string is 216 m s⁻¹.

parts.prompt: Calculate the wavelength of this n = 4 harmonic standing wave.
workingSteps: For a string fixed at both ends, λ_n = 2L / n.

parts.prompt: Determine the oscillation frequency of this standing wave.
Calculate the fundamental (first-harmonic) frequency of the string when kept at the same tension.

items.stem: A stationary racing telemetry drone emitting a steady acoustic tone emits a steady 640 Hz note in still air (speed of sound 340 m s⁻¹). If a camera car driving along the straightaway travels directly away from the source at 64 m s⁻¹, what frequency does it detect?
items.workedSolution: For a moving observer and stationary source, f′ = f(v − v_o) / v = 640 × (340 − 64) / 340 = 520 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates f′ = f(v − v_o) / v = 520 Hz (A).

items.stem: Figure shows a narrowband dye-laser beam striking a micro-machined silicon double-slit diaphragm directing monochromatic radiation of wavelength 633 nm at two slits with slit separation 0.55 mm. Across a screen at distance 3.4 m, an observer analyses the n = 4 bright interference fringe.
items.workedSolution: (a) Δℓ = nλ = 4 × 6.33 × 10⁻⁷ = 2.53 × 10⁻⁶ m. (b) θ_4 = arcsin(nλ / d) = 0.264°. (c) y_4 = nλD / d = 0.0157 m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

parts.prompt: Calculate the path difference between waves from S₁ and S₂ arriving at the n = 4 bright fringe.
workingSteps: For constructive interference at order n, Δℓ = nλ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular deflection θ_4 (in degrees) of the n = 4 bright fringe from the central axis.
Determine the linear distance from the central bright fringe to the n = 4 bright fringe on the screen.

items.stem: A continuous progressive wave in flexural waves travelling along a thin ribbon is investigated on a precision vibrating-reed actuator. Figure shows the spatial profile captured at a single instant, with amplitude 0.036 m and wavelength 1.2 m, driven continuously at 18 Hz.
items.workedSolution: (a) Period T = 1 / f = 1 / 18 = 0.0556 s. (b) Wave speed v = fλ = 18 × 1.2 = 21.6 m s⁻¹. (c) Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 113 rad s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies T = 1 / f with given frequency.
Substitutes into v = fλ or v = λ / T.

parts.prompt: Calculate the time period of oscillation of a point in the medium.
Determine the propagation speed of the progressive wave.
workingSteps: Apply v = fλ (or v = λ / T).

parts.prompt: Calculate the angular frequency ω of the wave oscillations.

items.stem: An acoustic resonator consists of a glass Kundt's open duct excited by a miniature loudspeaker near one rim of physical length 0.52 m. When excited in its n = 3 harmonic mode, displacement antinodes form at an end correction e = 0.025 m beyond each open end. The speed of sound in the air column is 340 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds twice the end correction: L_eff = L + 2e.

parts.prompt: Calculate the effective acoustic length L_eff between the two exterior antinodes.
workingSteps: An open-both-ends pipe has two open ends, so L_eff = L + 2e.

parts.prompt: Determine the wavelength of the n = 3 harmonic mode.
Calculate the resonant frequency of this standing wave.

items.stem: On an astronomical spectrograph test bench using a normal-incidence transmission grating with 400 lines mm⁻¹, the order n = 2 diffraction maximum of a monochromatic beam is measured at θ = 20.1° from the straight-through direction. What is the wavelength of the light?
items.workedSolution: Slit spacing d = 10⁻³ / 400 = 2.50 × 10⁻⁶ m. Rearranging d sin θ = nλ gives λ = d sin(20.1°) / 2 = 4.30 × 10⁻⁷ m.

markScheme.criterion: Computes d = 10⁻³ / N and λ = d sin θ / n = 4.30 × 10⁻⁷ m (A).

items.stem: Using a coastal oceanography telemetry buoy array, an acoustic wave-height gauge captures a progressive wave in regular swell waves across a test basin with amplitude 0.035 m, wavelength 0.24 m, and frequency 40 Hz. parts.prompt: Calculate the propagation speed of the wave.
Determine the oscillation period of particle P.
Calculate the phase difference, in radians, between the oscillations at P and Q.

items.stem: Monochromatic light of wavelength 488 nm passes through an adjustable micrometer razor-blade single slit illuminated normally by a collimated laser of slit width 0.25 mm onto a screen 1.8 m away. What is the full linear width of the central bright diffraction maximum on the screen?
items.workedSolution: First diffraction minima lie at θ = ±λ / b, giving half-width y₁ = λD / b = 3.51 × 10⁻³ m. Full central maximum width w = 2λD / b = 7.03 × 10⁻³ m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses w = 2λD / b to obtain 7.03 × 10⁻³ m (C).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by 4 instead of 2 when doubling the first-minimum half-width.

items.stem: On a microwave horn link employing parallel wire-grid polarizing frames, a plane-polarized beam of intensity 160 W m⁻² passes through an ideal linear analyzer, emerging with reduced intensity 131 W m⁻² (Malus's law: I = I₀ cos²θ). What acute angle θ is the analyzer's transmission axis rotated relative to the incident polarization?
items.workedSolution: From I = I₀ cos²θ, cos θ = √(131 / 160) = 0.906, giving θ = arccos(0.906) = 25.0°.

items.stem: Sound waves of speed 348 m s⁻¹ establish a stationary n = 3 odd-harmonic pattern inside a cylindrical clarinet-model bore closed at the reed end and open at the bell of effective length 0.28 m (assuming zero end correction).
items.workedSolution: (a) L_eff = 0.280 m, giving f₁ = v / (4L_eff) = 311 Hz. (b) λ_3 = 4L_eff / 3 = 0.373 m. (c) f_3 = 3f₁ = 932 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Applies quarter-wave fundamental relation f₁ = v / (4L_eff).
Multiplies fundamental frequency by odd harmonic index 3 (or uses v / λ).

parts.prompt: Calculate the fundamental (first-harmonic, n = 1) frequency of this closed-end air column.
workingSteps: For a pipe closed at one end, λ₁ = 4L so f₁ = v / (4L).

parts.prompt: Determine the wavelength of the n = 3 harmonic standing wave.
Calculate the resonant frequency of this n = 3 harmonic mode.

items.stem: Figure shows wavefronts radiated at 750 Hz by an autonomous test-track vehicle ultrasonic-audible beacon as it approaches directly towards a fixed acoustic array post at 88 m s⁻¹ (speed of sound 332 m s⁻¹). Calculate the observed acoustic frequency.
items.workedSolution: For a source moving towards a stationary observer, f' = fv / (v − v_s) = (750 × 332) / (332 − 88) = 1.02e+3 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Applies exact moving-source Doppler formula to obtain 1.02e+3 Hz (D).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the Doppler sign in the denominator, using v + v_s for an approaching source (or v − v_s for a receding source).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Applies the moving-observer equation f(v ± v_s) / v instead of the moving-source equation fv / (v ∓ v_s).

items.stem: In a darkroom optics experiment, a sodium vapour discharge lamp filtered and collimated onto a Young's double-slit plate emits coherent light of wavelength 612 nm onto a double slit of slit separation 0.16 mm, with an observation screen positioned 2.1 m away.
items.workedSolution: (a) Fringe spacing = λD / d = (6.12 × 10⁻⁷ × 2.1) / 1.60 × 10⁻⁴ = 8.03 × 10⁻³ m. (b) First dark fringe distance = ½ × 8.03 × 10⁻³ = 4.02 × 10⁻³ m. (c) At order n = 3, path difference = nλ = 3 × 6.12 × 10⁻⁷ = 1.84 × 10⁻⁶ m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

markScheme.criterion: Converts units and substitutes into λD / (slit separation).
Takes half of the bright-fringe spacing.

parts.prompt: Calculate the fringe spacing between adjacent bright fringes on the screen.
Determine the distance on the screen from the central bright maximum to the centre of the first dark fringe.
workingSteps: First destructive minimum occurs halfway between the central and first-order bright maxima: y_dark,1 = 0.5 × fringe spacing.

parts.prompt: Calculate the geometric path difference between waves arriving from the two slits at the order n = 3 bright fringe.
workingSteps: Constructive interference at order n requires path difference Δℓ = nλ.

items.stem: Unpolarized light of intensity 160 W m⁻² propagates along a photographic filter-transmission test bench with high-extinction linear polarizers through an ideal vertical polarizing sheet P₁ and a second sheet A whose axis makes θ = 35° with P₁ (polarized transmission obeys I = I₁ cos²θ).
items.workedSolution: (a) After P₁, I₁ = ½ I₀ = 80.0 W m⁻². (b) After analyzer A, I = I₁ cos²(35°) = 53.7 W m⁻². (c) Overall fraction I / I₀ = ½ cos²(35°) = 0.336.

markScheme.criterion: Halves unpolarized incident intensity at ideal polarizer P₁.
Applies I = I₁ cos²θ to the polarized beam.
Divides final transmitted intensity by incident unpolarized intensity I₀.

parts.prompt: State and calculate the intensity I₁ of the plane-polarized beam between polarizer P₁ and analyzer A.
workingSteps: Averaging cos²φ = ½ over all random polarization orientations reduces unpolarized intensity by half: I₁ = ½ I₀.

parts.prompt: Calculate the intensity I emerging from analyzer A.
workingSteps: Apply Malus's law I = I₁ cos²θ.

parts.prompt: Determine the overall fraction I / I₀ of the original unpolarized intensity transmitted by the two-filter combination.
workingSteps: Overall transmission fraction = I / I₀ = ½ cos²θ.

items.stem: On a laboratory sonometer, a brass harpsichord wire stretched between fixed hitch and wrest pins of length 1.25 m and mass per unit length 0.0032 kg m⁻¹ is held under a tension of 28.88 N. What is the frequency when it vibrates in harmonic mode n = 4?
items.workedSolution: Wave speed along the string is v = √(T / μ) = √(28.88 / 0.0032) = 95.0 m s⁻¹. For n = 4, f_n = nv / (2L) = 4 × 95.0 / (2 × 1.25) = 152 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates v = √(T / μ) and f_n = nv / (2L) = 152 Hz (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts tension and mass per unit length inside the radical, using √(μ / T).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in λ_n = 2L / n, computing (n / L)√(T / μ).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root over T / μ, computing (n / 2L)(T / μ).

items.stem: In a spectrometer experiment, a student goniometer spectrometer carrying a ruled glass diffraction grating (550 lines mm⁻¹) is illuminated perpendicularly by coherent light of wavelength 480 nm. Starting from order n = 1, a goniometer sweeps across −90° < θ < +90° to catalogue every observable principal maximum.
items.workedSolution: (a) d = 1.82 × 10⁻⁶ m, so θ₁ = arcsin(λ / d) = 15.3°. (b) d / λ = 3.79, giving n_max = 3. (c) Total principal maxima = 2(3) + 1 = 7.

markScheme.criterion: Computes d = 10⁻³ / N and applies sin θ₁ = λ / d.
Evaluates d / λ = 3.79 and rounds down.

parts.prompt: Calculate the diffraction angle (in degrees) of the first-order (n = 1) maximum.
Determine the maximum observable diffraction order n_max for this wavelength.
workingSteps: Since sin θ ≤ 1, truncate down: n_max = floor(3.79) = 3.

parts.prompt: State the total number of bright principal maxima formed across the forward semicircle.

items.stem: Coherent light of wavelength 514 nm from a collimated green DPSS diode-pumped laser directed normally onto two narrow parallel slits strikes a double slit of slit separation 0.375 mm placed 1.4 m from a screen. If the first diffraction-envelope minimum suppresses the n = 5 interference maximum, determine each slit's width b.
items.workedSolution: The first single-slit minimum occurs at θ = λ / b while the n-th double-slit maximum is at θ = nλ / d. Coincidence at n = 5 gives b = d / 5 = 3.75 × 10⁻⁴ / 5 = 7.50 × 10⁻⁵ m.

markScheme.criterion: Equates λ / b = nλ / d to obtain b = d / 5 = 7.50 × 10⁻⁵ m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides slit separation by (n + 1) instead of missing order n = d / b.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the highest visible order inside the central envelope (n − 1) instead of the missing order n.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Includes an erroneous factor of 2 from the full angular width of the central envelope.

items.stem: Figure shows a violin E-string tensioned across two hardwood vee-blocks on an optical bench of length 0.96 m vibrating in stationary harmonic mode n = 6 (wave speed 90 m s⁻¹). Determine the separation between consecutive nodes along the string.
items.workedSolution: In the n = 6 harmonic on a fixed string of length L = 0.96 m, n half-wavelength loops fit along L, so adjacent node spacing d_NN = λ / 2 = L / n = 0.96 / 6 = 0.160 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses d_NN = λ / 2 = L / n to obtain 0.160 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the node-to-adjacent-antinode distance λ / 4 instead of adjacent node spacing λ / 2.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides string length L by the total number of nodes (n + 1) instead of the number of loops n.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates a full wavelength λ = 2L / n instead of the half-wavelength node-to-node spacing λ / 2.

items.stem: A stationary high-speed sled mounted with an acoustic whistle emits a steady 580 Hz note in still air (speed of sound 340 m s⁻¹). If an instrumented chase cart on the parallel guideway travels directly away from the source at 78 m s⁻¹, what frequency does it detect?
items.workedSolution: For a moving observer and stationary source, f′ = f(v − v_o) / v = 580 × (340 − 78) / 340 = 447 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates f′ = f(v − v_o) / v = 447 Hz (A).

options.distractorRationale: Places observer speed in the denominator fv / (v ∓ v_o) as if the source were moving rather than the observer.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the observer Doppler sign in f(v ± v_o) / v.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the moving-source denominator formula AND reverses the Doppler sign.

items.stem: When a violet semiconductor laser beam incident perpendicular to a dual-slit foil slide of wavelength 460 nm illuminates two parallel slits at distance 2 m from a viewing screen, the distance from the central bright maximum to the n = 5 bright fringe is 25.6 mm. What is the slit separation?
items.workedSolution: Since y_n = nλD / d, slit separation d = nλD / y_n = (5 × 4.60 × 10⁻⁷ × 2) / 0.0256 = 1.80 × 10⁻⁴ m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Treats the n-th bright fringe displacement as a single fringe spacing, omitting the factor of n.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Applies dark-fringe factor (n − ½) instead of integer n.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides total span by (n + 1) instead of n fringe intervals between n = 0 and order n.

items.stem: On an ultrasonic non-destructive testing bench, a laser vibrometer scan captures a displacement–position profile for elastic shear waves in a polymer bar of amplitude 0.015 m and wavelength 0.8 m propagating at 68 m s⁻¹. What is the frequency of oscillation of the wave?
items.workedSolution: Using f = v / λ with wave speed v = 68 m s⁻¹ and wavelength λ = 0.8 m gives f = 68 / 0.8 = 85.0 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Rearranges v = fλ to obtain f = v / λ = 85.0 Hz (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the oscillation period T = λ / v instead of the frequency f = v / λ.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Mistakes two full cycles for one wavelength, halving the calculated frequency.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies wave speed by wavelength (vλ) instead of dividing v by λ.

items.stem: Figure illustrates a copper HVAC acoustic resonator duct open at each termination of length 0.42 m vibrating in harmonic mode n = 5 when the speed of sound is 343 m s⁻¹ (end correction negligible). Calculate the frequency emitted.
items.workedSolution: For an open pipe of length L = 0.42 m in harmonic n = 5, f_n = nv / (2L) = (5 × 343) / (2 × 0.42) = 2.04e+3 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes the fundamental frequency f₁ instead of the n-th harmonic.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses closed-one-end pipe relation nv / (4L) instead of open-both-ends nv / (2L).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in λ_n = 2L / n.

items.stem: On an astronomical spectrograph test bench using a normal-incidence transmission grating with 300 lines mm⁻¹, the order n = 2 diffraction maximum of a monochromatic beam is measured at θ = 20.7° from the straight-through direction. What is the wavelength of the light?
items.workedSolution: Slit spacing d = 10⁻³ / 300 = 3.33 × 10⁻⁶ m. Rearranging d sin θ = nλ gives λ = d sin(20.7°) / 2 = 5.89 × 10⁻⁷ m.

markScheme.criterion: Computes d = 10⁻³ / N and λ = d sin θ / n = 5.89 × 10⁻⁷ m (A).

items.stem: Along a marine towing-tank wave maker, monochromatic gravity waves along a channel of amplitude 0.045 m, wavelength 2 m, and frequency 10 Hz pass markers P at x₁ = 0.5 m and Q at x₂ = 1.8 m. What is the phase difference (in radians) between P and Q?
items.workedSolution: Separation Δx = 1.8 m − 0.5 m = 1.3 m. Cycle span = 2 m, giving 0.650 cycles. Phase difference Δφ = 2π × 0.650 = 4.08 rad.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates fractional cycle separation and multiplies by 2π rad to get 4.08 rad (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses half a cycle (π rad) instead of a full cycle (2π rad) in the phase-difference formula.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the fractional cycle ratio (dividing cycle span by separation instead of separation by cycle span).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes phase difference in degrees instead of radians.

items.stem: Figure shows a laser beam-expander test stage directing plane wavefronts onto a narrow vertical slit of aperture width 0.1 mm illuminated by coherent light of wavelength 514 nm, with a screen positioned 3.5 m behind the slit. Calculate the distance between the two first-order dark minima bounding the central maximum.
items.workedSolution: First diffraction minima lie at θ = ±λ / b, giving half-width y₁ = λD / b = 0.0180 m. Full central maximum width w = 2λD / b = 0.0360 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses w = 2λD / b to obtain 0.0360 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by slit width b and divides by screen distance D instead of 2λD / b.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates λD / b (the distance from the centre to one first-order minimum) instead of the full central maximum width 2λD / b.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by 4 instead of 2 when doubling the first-minimum half-width.

items.stem: On a photographic filter-transmission test bench with high-extinction linear polarizers, a plane-polarized beam of intensity 96 W m⁻² passes through an ideal linear analyzer, emerging with reduced intensity 78.9 W m⁻² (Malus's law: I = I₀ cos²θ). What acute angle θ is the analyzer's transmission axis rotated relative to the incident polarization?
items.workedSolution: From I = I₀ cos²θ, cos θ = √(78.9 / 96) = 0.906, giving θ = arccos(0.906) = 25.0°.

items.stem: In a resonance-tube determination of sound speed, a graduated laboratory resonance cylinder closed at the base and excited at the top rim of length 0.28 m (negligible end correction) resonates in its n = 7 odd harmonic when driven by a 1863 Hz source. What is the speed of sound in the tube?
items.workedSolution: For a closed-one-end pipe in odd harmonic n = 7, λ_n = 4L / n = 4(0.28) / 7 = 0.177 m. Speed of sound v = f_n λ_n = 330 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v = 4Lf_n / n to obtain 330 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses open-pipe wavelength 2L / n instead of closed-pipe 4L / n, halving the speed of sound.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes an even harmonic index (n − 1) instead of the odd harmonic n.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Treats the n-th harmonic frequency as the fundamental mode v = 4Lf.

items.stem: Sounding continuously at 560 Hz, an express electric locomotive horn recedes directly away from a commuter standing beside the straight track through still air (speed of sound 343 m s⁻¹). If the stationary observer records a shifted frequency of 467 Hz, what is the speed of the source?
items.workedSolution: Rearranging f' = fv / (v + v_s) gives v + v_s = vf / f' = (343 × 560) / 467, yielding v_s = 68.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Solves f' = fv / (v ∓ v_s) for v_s = 68.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.distractorRationale: Halves the source speed as if applying a two-way radar reflection formula.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the low-speed / moving-observer relation v|f'/f − 1| instead of rearranging the exact moving-source formula f' = fv / (v ∓ v_s).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Stops at the effective denominator speed v(f / f') without taking the difference from v.

items.stem: Using a narrowband dye-laser beam striking a micro-machined silicon double-slit diaphragm with a slit separation of 0.2 mm and a slit-to-screen distance of 1.8 m, the measured fringe spacing between adjacent bright fringes is 3.65 mm. What is the wavelength of the light?
items.workedSolution: Rearranging fringe spacing Δy = λD / d gives λ = Δy × d / D = (3.64 × 10⁻³ × 2.00 × 10⁻⁴) / 1.8 = 4.05 × 10⁻⁷ m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

markScheme.criterion: Rearranges double-slit relation to obtain λ = 4.05 × 10⁻⁷ m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Introduces a spurious factor of ½ from single-slit central-width formulas.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats bright-to-bright fringe spacing as half-wavelength path difference.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies fringe spacing by screen distance D and divides by slit separation instead of multiplying by slit separation / D.

items.stem: Figure shows unpolarized radiation of intensity 220 W m⁻² on an optical bench fitted with a Glan-Thompson calcite polarizer and a rotatable analyzer passing sequentially through polarizer P₁ and analyzer An inclined at θ = 25° relative to P₁ (Malus's law for polarized light: I = I₁ cos²θ). Calculate the final transmitted intensity.
items.workedSolution: Ideal polarizer P₁ transmits half of the unpolarized intensity: I₁ = ½ I₀ = 110 W m⁻². Analyzer A then transmits I = I₁ cos²(25°) = ½(220) cos²(25°) = 90.4 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Applies I = ½ I₀ cos²(25°) = 90.4 W m⁻² (B).

items.stem: On a laboratory sonometer, a cello A-string held taut between the fingerboard nut and tailpiece bridge of length 0.9 m and mass per unit length 0.0015 kg m⁻¹ is held under a tension of 51.34 N. What is the frequency when it vibrates in harmonic mode n = 3?
items.workedSolution: Wave speed along the string is v = √(T / μ) = √(51.3375 / 0.0015) = 185 m s⁻¹. For n = 3, f_n = nv / (2L) = 3 × 185 / (2 × 0.9) = 308 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates v = √(T / μ) and f_n = nv / (2L) = 308 Hz (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts tension and mass per unit length inside the radical, using √(μ / T).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in λ_n = 2L / n, computing (n / L)√(T / μ).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root over T / μ, computing (n / 2L)(T / μ).

items.stem: Figure shows a discharge-lamp spectroscopy setup where collimated monochromatic light strikes a grating normally (350 lines mm⁻¹) illuminated perpendicularly by monochromatic light of wavelength 595 nm. Determine the maximum observable order n_max.
items.workedSolution: Grating spacing d = 10⁻³ / 350 = 2.86 × 10⁻⁶ m. Since sin θ ≤ 1, n ≤ d / λ = 2.86 × 10⁻⁶ / 5.95 × 10⁻⁷ = 4.80. Taking the floor gives n_max = 4.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates d / λ = 4.80 and takes floor to get n_max = 4 (A).

items.stem: Using a helium-neon gas laser illuminating a precision photo-etched double slit of wavelength 650 nm at screen distance 2.2 m, two parallel slits each of individual slit width 0.08 mm are separated by centre-to-centre slit separation 0.4 mm. Which positive interference order n is the first missing order due to single-slit diffraction?
items.workedSolution: Interference maxima satisfy sin θ = nλ / d and the first single-slit minimum satisfies sin θ = λ / b. Dividing gives n = d / b = 4.00 × 10⁻⁴ / 8.00 × 10⁻⁵ = 5.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Selects the last bright interference order visible inside one side of the central envelope (d/b − 1) instead of the missing order d/b.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Counts the total number of bright fringes inside the central diffraction envelope (2d/b − 1) instead of the missing order index.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles d / b by using full angular width 2λ / b instead of first-minimum angle λ / b.

items.stem: When a steel acoustic-guitar treble string mounted between a nut and bridge saddle of length 0.48 m vibrates in its n = 3 stationary-wave harmonic, a stroboscope measures its frequency as 337.5 Hz. Determine the wave speed along the wire.
items.workedSolution: For harmonic n = 3 on a string of length L = 0.48 m fixed at both ends, λ_n = 2L / n = 2(0.48) / 3 = 0.320 m. Wave speed v = f_n λ_n = 337.5 × 0.320 = 108 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes λ_n = 2L / n and v = f_n λ_n = 108 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses λ_n = L / n instead of 2L / n, underestimating wave speed by a factor of 2.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Applies the closed-pipe boundary relation 4L / n instead of fixed-string 2L / n.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Treats the harmonic frequency as the fundamental mode (omitting division by n).

items.stem: A stationary autonomous test-track vehicle ultrasonic-audible beacon radiates sound at 920 Hz in still air (speed of sound 343 m s⁻¹). Meanwhile, a second instrumented test vehicle on the straight lane travels directly towards the source and measures a frequency of 1.11e+3 Hz. What is the speed of the moving observer?
items.workedSolution: For a stationary source and moving observer, f′ = f(v + v_o) / v. Rearranging gives v_o = v|f′ / f − 1| = 343 × |1.11e+3 / 920 − 1| = 72.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses f′ = f(v ± v_o) / v to obtain v_o = 72.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

options.distractorRationale: Divides the speed by 2 as if solving a two-way pulse-echo Doppler shift.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Applies the moving-source algebra v|1 − f / f'| instead of the moving-observer relation v|f' / f − 1|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the wave speed relative to the observer (v ± v_o) without subtracting the speed of sound v.

items.stem: When a blue gallium-nitride laser module aligned along an optical rail toward two parallel slits of wavelength 460 nm illuminates two parallel slits at distance 3 m from a viewing screen, the distance from the central bright maximum to the n = 4 bright fringe is 15.8 mm. What is the slit separation?
items.workedSolution: Since y_n = nλD / d, slit separation d = nλD / y_n = (4 × 4.60 × 10⁻⁷ × 3) / 0.0158 = 3.50 × 10⁻⁴ m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Treats the n-th bright fringe displacement as a single fringe spacing, omitting the factor of n.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Applies dark-fringe factor (n − ½) instead of integer n.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides total span by (n + 1) instead of n fringe intervals between n = 0 and order n.

items.stem: In an investigation with a precision vibrating-reed actuator, flexural waves travelling along a thin ribbon of amplitude 0.06 m have a crest-to-crest wavelength of 0.4 m while the oscillator operates at 85 Hz. At what speed do the wavefronts travel?
items.workedSolution: From the displacement–position profile, wavelength λ = 0.4 m and frequency f = 85 Hz. Using the wave equation v = fλ = 85 Hz × 0.4 m = 34.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies v = fλ to obtain 34.0 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides wavelength by frequency (λ / f), confusing frequency f with period T.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the wavelength by misreading a two-cycle span as a single wavelength.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides frequency by wavelength (f / λ) instead of applying v = fλ.

items.stem: In an acoustics test, a copper HVAC acoustic resonator duct open at each termination has physical length 0.48 m, and each open end introduces an antinode end correction of 0.02 m. If the speed of sound is 340 m s⁻¹, what is the resonant frequency of the n = 2 harmonic?
items.workedSolution: Because the pipe is open at both ends, effective acoustic length L_eff = L + 2e = 0.48 + 2(0.02) = 0.520 m. For n = 2, λ_n = 2L_eff / n = 0.520 m, so f_n = v / λ_n = 340 / 0.520 = 654 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses the closed-pipe denominator 4L_eff instead of the open-pipe 2L_eff.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds only one end correction (L + e) instead of accounting for both open ends (L + 2e).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Ignores the acoustic end corrections completely, using physical length L instead of L + 2e.

items.stem: Monochromatic light of wavelength 589 nm strikes a discharge-lamp spectroscopy setup where collimated monochromatic light strikes a grating normally ruled with 500 lines mm⁻¹. At what angle θ from the normal is the order n = 1 principal maximum observed?
items.workedSolution: Grating spacing d = 10⁻³ / 500 = 2.00 × 10⁻⁶ m. Using d sin θ = nλ gives sin θ = (1 × 5.89 × 10⁻⁷) / 2.00 × 10⁻⁶ = 0.294, so θ = 17.1°.

markScheme.criterion: Converts d = 10⁻³ / N and solves d sin θ = nλ to get 17.1° (C).

items.stem: On a geotechnical seismic array, a linear geophone line logs a sinusoidal displacement–time graph of period 0.2 s and amplitude 0.045 m for a wave moving at 1.2 m s⁻¹. Determine the wavelength of this progressive wave.
items.workedSolution: From the displacement–time trace, the period is T = 0.2 s. Using λ = vT with v = 1.2 m s⁻¹ gives λ = 1.2 × 0.2 = 0.240 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses λ = vT = 1.2 m s⁻¹ × 0.2 s to obtain 0.240 m (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides period by wave speed (T / v) instead of multiplying vT.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Reads the full two-cycle time span 2T as a single period when computing λ = vT.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides wave speed by period (v / T), treating period T on the time axis as if it were frequency f.

items.stem: Monochromatic light of wavelength 633 nm passes through a laser beam-expander test stage directing plane wavefronts onto a narrow vertical slit of slit width 0.15 mm onto a screen 3 m away. What is the full linear width of the central bright diffraction maximum on the screen?
items.workedSolution: First diffraction minima lie at θ = ±λ / b, giving half-width y₁ = λD / b = 0.0127 m. Full central maximum width w = 2λD / b = 0.0253 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses w = 2λD / b to obtain 0.0253 m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by slit width b and divides by screen distance D instead of 2λD / b.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates λD / b (the distance from the centre to one first-order minimum) instead of the full central maximum width 2λD / b.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by 4 instead of 2 when doubling the first-minimum half-width.

items.stem: On a stress-photoelasticity polariscope bench with graduated rotary analyzer mount, a plane-polarized beam of intensity 160 W m⁻² passes through an ideal linear analyzer, emerging with reduced intensity 40.0 W m⁻² (Malus's law: I = I₀ cos²θ). What acute angle θ is the analyzer's transmission axis rotated relative to the incident polarization?
items.workedSolution: From I = I₀ cos²θ, cos θ = √(40.0 / 160) = 0.500, giving θ = arccos(0.500) = 60.0°.

items.stem: Figure illustrates a Kundt's acoustic tube fitted with a rigid brass piston at one end and open at the other of length 0.52 m excited in its n = 7 odd harmonic mode (speed of sound 330 m s⁻¹, end correction negligible). What is the frequency of the sound wave?
items.workedSolution: Effective acoustic length for one closed and one open end is L_eff = L + e = 0.520 m. For odd harmonic n = 7, f_n = nv / (4L_eff) = (7 × 330) / (4 × 0.520) = 1.11e+3 Hz.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the n = 1 fundamental frequency v / (4L).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes the prohibited even harmonic (n − 1) into nv / (4L).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Applies open-both-ends formula nv / (2L) instead of closed-one-end nv / (4L).

items.stem: Emitting a continuous tone of frequency 900 Hz, an emergency ambulance siren recedes directly away from a stationary roadside acoustic logger at a constant speed of 60 m s⁻¹. Taking the speed of sound in still air as 332 m s⁻¹, what frequency is detected by the stationary observer?
items.workedSolution: For a source moving away from a stationary observer, f' = fv / (v + v_s) = (900 × 332) / (332 + 60) = 762 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Applies exact moving-source Doppler formula to obtain 762 Hz (B).

options.distractorRationale: Applies the moving-observer equation f(v ± v_s) / v instead of the moving-source equation fv / (v ∓ v_s).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the moving-observer formula AND reverses the sign of the Doppler frequency shift.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the Doppler sign in the denominator, using v + v_s for an approaching source (or v − v_s for a receding source).

items.stem: Coherent monochromatic light of wavelength 532 nm from a collimated green DPSS diode-pumped laser directed normally onto two narrow parallel slits strikes a double slit with slit separation 0.6 mm and forms fringes on a screen 3.6 m behind the barrier. Determine the bright-to-bright fringe spacing.
items.workedSolution: Converting to SI units: λ = 5.32 × 10⁻⁷ m and slit separation = 6.00 × 10⁻⁴ m. Fringe spacing = λD / (slit separation) = (5.32 × 10⁻⁷ × 3.6) / 6.00 × 10⁻⁴ = 3.19 × 10⁻³ m. (In NCUK/A-Level notation, w = λD / s where w is fringe spacing and s is slit separation.)

markScheme.criterion: Uses fringe spacing = λD / (slit separation) to obtain 3.19 × 10⁻³ m (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by slit separation and divides by screen distance (λd / D) instead of λD / d.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the distance from the central bright fringe to the first dark minimum (½ λD / d) instead of bright fringe spacing.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Includes an erroneous factor of 2, confusing double-slit fringe spacing with single-slit central maximum width.

items.stem: Unpolarized light of intensity 64 W m⁻² enters a fibre-optics free-space polarization controller bench with an ideal linear analyzer, passing first through an ideal vertical polarizer P₁ and then through an ideal analyzer A whose axis is rotated by 70° to P₁ (for plane-polarized light of intensity I₁, analyzer transmission is I = I₁ cos²θ). What intensity emerges from analyzer A?
items.workedSolution: Ideal polarizer P₁ transmits half of the unpolarized intensity: I₁ = ½ I₀ = 32.0 W m⁻². Analyzer A then transmits I = I₁ cos²(70°) = ½(64) cos²(70°) = 3.74 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Applies I = ½ I₀ cos²(70°) = 3.74 W m⁻² (A).

items.stem: Figure shows a brass harpsichord wire stretched between fixed hitch and wrest pins of vibrating length 0.5 m and linear density 0.0015 kg m⁻¹ tensioned at 18.15 N. Calculate the resonant frequency of harmonic mode n = 3.
items.workedSolution: Wave speed along the string is v = √(T / μ) = √(18.15 / 0.0015) = 110 m s⁻¹. For n = 3, f_n = nv / (2L) = 3 × 110 / (2 × 0.5) = 330 Hz.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates v = √(T / μ) and f_n = nv / (2L) = 330 Hz (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts tension and mass per unit length inside the radical, using √(μ / T).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2 in λ_n = 2L / n, computing (n / L)√(T / μ).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root over T / μ, computing (n / 2L)(T / μ).

items.stem: A laser beam of wavelength 580 nm is incident normally on a holographic polymer grating slide illuminated at normal incidence on an optical rail with 300 lines mm⁻¹. Including the central zero-order beam, how many total principal maxima emerge across the forward semicircle (−90° ≤ θ ≤ +90°)?
items.workedSolution: d = 10⁻³ / 300 = 3.33 × 10⁻⁶ m, so d / λ = 5.75 and n_max = 5. Including ±1..±5 and n = 0 gives 2(5) + 1 = 11 principal maxima.
